stories.title: Knicks waive Bruce Brown, expected to sign James Wiseman for final roster spot
stories.summary: The Knicks announced they have waived Bruce Brown, with center James Wiseman expected to capture the team's final roster spot ahead of the season opener.
stories.detailText: The Knicks were unable to finalize a trade to make room on the roster and were forced to waive guard Bruce Brown ahead of the regular season, the team announced Saturday. New York liked Brown, who survived preseason cuts following Thursday's preseason finale, but it needed to trade a player on a standard contract to remain below the second apron if it wanted to keep both Brown and James Wiseman -- the final roster spot selection. Unfortunately, the Knicks couldn't find a trade partner. It wasn't for a lack of trying, though. SNY's Ian Begley reported earlier in the week that New York would "explore all avenues" to keep Brown and Wiseman and mentioned that it was "logical to assume" that Pacome Dadiet would be a player the Knicks would try to move. Tyler Kolek 's name was also mentioned as a possible trade candidate. Since New York couldn't send any money in a deal, it needed to include draft picks (the Knicks have 11 second-round picks over the next seven drafts). But even that substantial capital wasn't enough to make a trade, which meant New York had to say goodbye to Brown. In theory, the Knicks could still make a trade after the first game and then bring Brown back. But for the season opener, Brown will not be a Knick Brown, 30, has played eight NBA seasons with six different teams, most recently with the Denver Nuggets, where he averaged 7.9 points and 2.1 assists in 24.4 minutes per game. In preseason with the Knicks, the veteran saw action in three games (one start) and totaled 11 points, five rebounds and three assists across 38 minutes on the court. Wiseman saw action in four preseason games with the Knicks and combined for 32 points and 17 rebounds in 46 minutes. He also added three blocks. His best game came in his lone start against the Toronto Raptors, where he had a double-double (18 points, 10 rebounds) in 24 minutes. A former No. 2 overall pick by the Golden State Warriors in the 2020 NBA Draft, Wiseman got off to a strong start with the Warriors before a severe knee injury cost him a year and a half and derailed his career. He returned to Golden State in 2022-23 in a much more limited role before he was traded to the Detroit Pistons, where he excelled once again for the remainder of the season. Following another year with the Pistons as a bench player, Wiseman joined the Indiana Pacers but tore his Achilles in the first game of the season and was out for the year. Last season, Wiseman played in just four games. Still, at just 25 years old, the Knicks saw potential in the 6-foot-11 big man and signed him to an Exhibit 9 contract prior to training camp and he impressed enough during the preseason to beat out players like Drew Eubanks and Tony Bradley .

stories.title: Evan Mobley impresses in Cavs annual Wine & Gold scrimmage
stories.summary: “Evan was elite.”
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND, OH - OCTOBER 11: Evan Mobley #4 of the Cleveland Cavaliers is introduced before the game against the Orlando Magic during a 2026 NBA Preseason game on October 11, 2026 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, Ohio. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Joe Murphy/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images CLEVELAND — The Cleveland Cavaliers held their annual Wine & Gold scrimmage in front of season ticket holders at Public Auditorium on Saturday morning. Head coach Kenny Atkinson has mentioned throughout preseason that he was treating this event as the fourth exhibition game, and he was true to his word. The Cavs split into two teams, played a 36-minute game, and had regular NBA refs. So while this wasn’t an official preseason game, it was their final dress rehearsal before the season tips off on Thursday. The starters for each team are below. It’s worth pointing out that Sam Merrill, Nae’Qwan Tomlin, and Khalifa Diop did not participate. Wine Gold Donovan Mitchell James Harden Meleek Thomas Tyrese Proctor Jaylon Tyson Craig Porter Jr. Mario Hezonja Peyton Watson Jarrett Allen Evan Mobley Gold dominated this game from start to finish, winning 96-82. They jumped out to an early lead thanks to strong showings from Harden and Mobley. Wine couldn’t contain the Harden and Mobley pick-and-roll, which led to easy paint touches for Mobley and his teammates. Wine’s perimeter defense struggled throughout. And while Mitchell did his part offensively, it wasn’t enough to make the game competitive down the stretch. “I felt like they were giving up layup after layup after layup and then paint points and it’s like, at a certain point, you gotta him them and make them aware that’s not acceptable,” Atkinson said afterward. There were no official stats, but the consensus was that Mobley was the leading scorer. He hit a few threes, attacked the basket continually, and overall had a strong all-around game. “Evan was elite,” Atkinson said. Atkinson singled out Harden and Mitchell for having good games, but he was quick to point out that Mitchell was part of Wine’s defense, which was a problem. Tyson also got a mention from Atkinson afterwards for his offensive production. The game wasn’t the only noteworthy thing that took place at Public Auditorium on Saturday. At halftime, several fans and some members of the Cavs participated in a half-court conference. Porter and Allen missed their attempts, but Atkinson nailed a half-court shot as the final contestant. The #Cavs held a halfcourt shot contest for $10k during the Wine and Gold Scrimmage. When no one could make it, players started trying. Then head coach Kenny Atkinson stepped up and nailed his attempt, winning all 20 contestants $500 gift cards and getting his team hyped 😂 pic.twitter.com/VQFFo011T2 — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) October 17, 2026 After the game, rookies Thomas and Ernest Udeh Jr. were forced to sing karaoke. #Cavs Meleek Thomas and Ernest Udeh Jr. gave the Wine and Gold Scrimmage crowd a show for their rookie performance, singing Katy Perry's "California Gurls" 😂 pic.twitter.com/4E6jeFU1tK — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) October 17, 2026 Support us and rep the Guardians with Homage! Anything bought from the links helps support Fear the Sword . You can buy the Guardians throwback shirt HERE . You can also shop all of Homage’s Cleveland gear HERE . You don’t want to take too much from a scrimmage that some guys wore sweatpants in, but there were a few observations worth pointing out. First, this was the best Mobley has played this preseason . Offensively, he effectively attacked off the dribble by pushing the ball off live rebounds and operating at the top of the arc in isolation. This was on top of doing a good job defensively of keeping Wine from getting to the rim. Most importantly, Mobley looked comfortable paired with Harden . “I like it,” Mobley said when asked about playing alongside Harden more. “I think we’re trying to build a lot of two-man games and more camaraderie. I like the play that we had, and I think the more that we play together, we’re just going to have more and more chemistry.” Mobley’s two-man game with Harden was impressive . Mobley did a good job making contact on the screen and rolling hard in the pick-and-roll. Both of which are necessary to create space when paired with Harden. The duo also ran a few inverted pick-and-rolls with Harden as the screener that produced good results. “James has been great in pick-and-rolls and setting up big men for a long time,” Mobley said. “I love what I’m seeing from Evan and James,” Atkinson echoed. “[They’re] really starting to get on the same page. I think that’s part of Evan being in the paint more. James missed him a few times at the rim today, but the intent is there.” Atkinson has hinted throughout preseason that he’ll start the season pairing Harden and Mobley together. Figuring out the right other three guys to play around them is important as well to that group’s success . “Because Evan can stretch [the floor] a little bit, you don’t have to be as intentional about the shooting piece,” Atkinson said when asked what is needed from the other three players in those lineups. “I think you can throw any three guys out there.” While any three guys might work, Watson is a seamless fit alongside Harden and Mobley . There were several times the defense was able to cut off the pick-and-roll, which forced the ball out to Watson on either the weak-side wing or corner. That set him up for a few catch-and-shoot threes that he knocked down. More importantly, Watson also showed that he can put the ball on the ground and create his own shot. That last part has the potential to be extremely helpful against opponents that sell out to stop the Harden and Mobley pick-and-roll. Thomas seems much more comfortable creating offense off-ball . The rookie got to his spots on the court when he wasn’t playing alongside Mitchell, but he struggled to have that same impact when he was featured more off-ball. The Cavs are still trying to figure out what lineups Thomas can be most effective in. “He’s really good on the ball,” Atkinson said. “We’re just trying to find that right balance.” Atkinson thinks that Thomas could be a good pairing alongside Mitchell. He wants to see Thomas play more of the role Dennis Schroder did alongside Mitchell last season. In those lineups, Mitchell was able to shift off-ball. Grouping Mitchell and Thomas together might also work due to how they’ve connected off the court . “Donovan has taken a special liking to Maleek,” Atkinson said. “He almost feels like ‘I have to build that relationship, build that trust, and then coach them up.’ I always say, player development coaches get way too much credit. It’s having really good, smart vets that elevate guys. We do our little part, and I think we put them in the right places, but it’s really the coaching from your best players that elevates younger players.”

stories.title: Owner Tom Dundon says keeping Trail Blazers in Portand 'is the priority'
stories.summary: The Trail Blazers and the City of Portland are in negotiations over Moda Center renovations and a new lease.
stories.detailText: Earlier this week, in what can only be described as an encouraging sign, Trail Blazers owner Tom Dundon met with City of Portland representatives after a Trail Blazers preseason game. Those two sides are negotiating Moda Center renovations and a new lease for the team that extends out 20 years. Earlier this summer, it would have been polite to call those negotiations "contentious," with a veiled threat of team relocation hanging over the talks, but the temperature appears to have cooled down. Another good sign, what Dundon told Mike Vorkunov of The Athletic . "We are working to keep the team in Portland," Dundon said by text message. "That is the priority." It hasn't always felt that way to Trail Blazers faithful/ Dundon's numerous penny-pinching moves since taking over the Trail Blazers have been an embarrassment and reminded people what they dislike most about private equity and billionaires. The most recent example was lowballing and pushing out the door beloved and elite television play-by-play man Kevin Calabro, hiring but not properly vetting 29-year-old replacement Braiden Bell, then firing Bell less than 24 hours later after old mysognistic/racists social media posts came to light, then eventually hiring Trail Blazers radio veteran Travis Demers but only on a temporary, game-by-game or trial basis. Even if the Trail Blazers eventually landed in the right place, they embarrassed themselves getting there. Part of the concern about Dundon was that this was the movie Major League come to life — he was making moves to frustrate the fan base so he could move the team to a place he felt was a friendlier business environment. That was also always going to be a far more difficult process in reality than it was on paper. "I want to be very direct about it: I would see it as a failure if we did not keep the team in Portland," NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said this summer. "I've spent a lot of time in that community over the years. They've shown amazing support for the Trail Blazers. They're some of our best fans around the league." Still, it's a negotiation between the Trail Blazers and Portland. While a series of government agencies at the state, county and city level have stepped forward with nearly $600 million for needed Moda Center renovations, the terms of the renovations and new lease with the city had sticking points. Among them: • A $3 million annual rent charge. • The City of Portland gets a 6% tax on each game ticket sold as well as every parking fee at the building. The team believes this is too high. • The city wants the Trail Blazers to agree to hire union workers for the renovations and construction process, as well as for concession workers on game night. • The Trail Blazers want increased security in and around the arena on game night and for the city to pay for that. The sides are talking, and the public rhetoric seems to have cooled, which is a good sign. The deadline is the end of the year, when the state money dedicated to the renovations would go away. Like most negotiations, don't be surprised if this one goes down to the wire.

stories.title: LeBron James describes helicopter commute from New York to Philadelphia as 'just another way of transportation'
stories.summary: James' helicopter arrangement is reportedly part of his deal with Fanatics.
stories.detailText: LeBron James has been commuting from New York to Philadelphia 76ers practices and games. And he's been doing so by helicopter. "Yeah, I've done it before," the 41-year-old James said, via ESPN's Kris Rhim , when asked about the arrangement after the Sixers' preseason finale on Friday. "Just another way of transportation. Yeah, that's all." LeBron James on his helicopter travel: “I’ve done it before, just another mode of transportation.” pic.twitter.com/0yLAr1Rr0N — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) October 17, 2026 Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season While James spoke about his travel setup for the first time in the wake of a 125-120 overtime loss to the Boston Celtics, it's been a topic of conversation for a while. After all, he's one of the basketball greats, and he's playing in his NBA-record-extending 24th season . Front Office Sports reported earlier this month that James flying back and forth from New York to Philly is part of his deal with Fanatics, a sports platform known for its apparel business. James has been using the company's aviation, a privilege afforded to him after he signed a multi-year trading card partnership with Fanatics in January 2024, according to the Oct. 5 FOS report. James' travel time is more than halved when he flies by helicopter, compared to driving from New York to Philly. It's estimated to take him between 30 and 45 minutes. "The deal we signed with Fanatics almost three years ago includes access to their corporate aviation," a spokesperson for James told FOS. "It's a feature in many of their deals with their largest athletes and we appreciate their partnership as LeBron splits his time between New York and Philadelphia." Although James has promoted Fanatics for years through his partnership with the company, his helicopter perk has been stirring up conversation due to his current NBA situation. After leaving the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency, James signed a team-friendly deal with the Sixers, more specifically a two-year contract reportedly worth only $8 million. Fanatics, notably, is owned by Michael Rubin, who sold his shares of Sixers ownership in 2022. At this point, any perceived conflict of interest seems to be the result of conjecture, but investigative journalist Pablo Torre told FOS recently that he and his team were "looking into all of the ways that is both a good story as well as something that is of interest to the league." He added: "And, by the way, it may not be the latter; it does appear to be the former as a business story." Torre then released an episode of his show, "Pablo Torre Finds Out," on Thursday addressing the subject. Torre dove into the details surrounding the Fanatics helicopter in question and noted that he had been told league sources have wondered whether Rubin convinced James to sign with the Sixers at Fanatics Fest in mid-July . But Torre went on to say, "This is not me alleging this is cap circumvention; it is, though, me pointing out, this is pretty funny." He continued: "It is a pretty funny series of apparent coincidences for a helicopter that lots of people have been asking questions about." It's possible the hoopla is much ado about nothing. James' tone when answering the question about his helicopter rides on Friday certainly suggests he thinks so. The Sixers' regular season begins on Tuesday in New York, as James and Co. will take on the defending NBA champion Knicks in Madison Square Garden.

stories.title: LeBron plays down concerns over helicopter commute, 'just another way of transportation'
stories.summary: LeBron chose to play for the 76ers, that's a little different from choosing Philadelphia.
stories.detailText: Let's be honest with ourselves: Part of the concern basketball fans have with LeBron James' helicopter commute to Philadelphia games and practices is a shared PTSD from the tragic death of Kobe Bryant. Those emotional scars remain. While fans in Philadelphia and beyond have made a big deal of LeBron commuting from a home in New York to Philadelphia via helicopter, his comments downplayed it, via Tony Jones at The Athletic . "Yeah, I've done it before," James said. "Just another, just another way of transportation. That's all." LeBron has been using a helicopter — provided by the sports apparel company Fanatics, according to Pablo Torre Finds Out — to commute from New York to the 76ers practice facility in Camden, N.J. As the Dan LeBatard show pointed out , LeBron chose the 76ers, not Philadelphia. For Philly fans, that's not much of a distinction, but it is one. LeBron isn't the first person to do this commute, as noted by Jones former 76ers guard and current Lakers coach JJ Redick used to live in New York, although he hired a car service to do it. That drive is around two hours (more on bad traffic days), by helicopter, it's more like half an hour. LeBron isn't changing his plans, and he is unconcerned about the discourse around his commute. Check out LeBron's official debut as a 76er on Tuesday when he makes a shorter commute to Madison Square Garden with his teammates for the season opener, trying to spoil ring night for Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks, a game you can watch on NBC and Peacock. It's the anchor game of a triple-header — Celtics at Pistons at 3 p.m. Eastern, and Thunder at Spurs at 9:30 p.m. Eastern — with all the games shown on NBC and streaming on Peacock.

stories.title: Suns waive Haywood Highsmith and retain Jamaree Bouyea
stories.summary: Phoenix is retaining Bouyea over Highsmith, prioritizing youth, development, and flexibility ahead of opening night.
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MI - OCTOBER 5: Haywood Highsmith #19 of the Phoenix Suns handles the ball during the game against the Detroit Pistons during a preseason game on October 5, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The roster fine-tuning has begun for the Phoenix Suns as they prepare for the 2026–27 season, and I have a feeling some of the more analytical members of the fan base aren’t going to be particularly happy with the latest decision. After being claimed off waivers following his release from the Brooklyn Nets last season, Haywood Highsmith has officially been cut by Phoenix, with the organization opting to retain Jamaree Bouyea instead. The Phoenix Suns are keeping Jamaree Bouyea as the 14th player on the roster. They have officialy cut Haywood Highsmith. — John Gambadoro (@Gambo987) October 17, 2026 Both Highsmith and Bouyea carry non-guaranteed contracts that don’t become fully guaranteed until January 27. Highsmith appeared in seven games for the Suns last season, averaging 5.4 points in 13 minutes per contest. He also appeared in two postseason games, failing to score in either appearance. At nearly 30 years old, Highsmith profiles as a quality three-and-D player. Although he stands 6’5”, he possesses tremendous length and has carved out a place in the NBA through toughness, grit, and his ability to knock down shots. He’s the type of player who has earned everything he’s received throughout his professional career. But when you look at the current state of the Phoenix Suns, there are several factors that likely influenced this decision. First, the Suns simply appear to like Bouyea more. He’s somebody the organization identified while he was playing in the G League with the Austin Spurs, brought into the fold, and continued developing. And he’s rewarded that investment with some encouraging performances, including a strong preseason in which he averaged 9.8 points in 16.6 minutes across five games. So Phoenix is opting to retain a player who’s three years younger and whom the organization has already identified as somebody worth continuing to develop. Bouyea also provides additional depth at the guard position, which brings us to another reason Highsmith became expendable. The Suns have plenty of depth on the wing, particularly when you consider the number of young players who need opportunities to develop. Ryan Dunn, Rasheer Fleming, and Koa Peat are all players the organization has invested in, and finding meaningful minutes for Highsmith would potentially mean prioritizing his playing time over the development of those prospects. For a team that’s attempting to build toward the future while remaining competitive in the present, that becomes an important consideration. The third factor is Highsmith’s injury history. There are legitimate concerns surrounding his health following the meniscus tear he suffered last season, and it’s fair to wonder whether he’s fully recovered. From the organization’s perspective, maintaining flexibility rather than committing to a player whose availability could remain uncertain might be the more appealing approach. Which brings us to the fourth reason I believe this transaction occurred. The Phoenix Suns have demonstrated a preference for maintaining optionality and roster flexibility, particularly at the beginning of a season, rather than filling every available roster spot simply because they can. Releasing Highsmith opens one roster spot for Phoenix. Could that spot eventually be occupied by Duop Reath? Certainly. But my assumption is that Reath will ultimately land on a two-way contract alongside Koby Brea and Pat Spencer. I think the Suns would prefer to keep that 15th roster spot available because, quite frankly, they don’t fully know who they are yet. There’s still plenty to learn about this roster, how the rotations will develop, and what needs might emerge once the regular season begins. So you let the season play out, evaluate what you have, and when the time comes, if there’s a player who can address a specific need, you have the flexibility to make that move. That’s the value of maintaining options rather than committing to a roster spot simply for the sake of filling it. Ultimately, this decision says more about the Suns’ priorities than it does about Highsmith’s ability to contribute. Phoenix is choosing youth, development, and flexibility over a veteran whose opportunities were already going to be limited. Bouyea gets another chance to prove he belongs, while the front office maintains the ability to address needs as they emerge. There’s value in that approach, especially for a team still figuring out what it has. Sometimes the smartest roster move is knowing when to leave a spot open.

stories.title: What we learned from the Lakers' preseason games and training camp
stories.summary: The Lakers' big three of Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler only played one half together in five preseason games, giving many others opportunities.
stories.detailText: Lakers head coach JJ Redick has not committed to his starting five for the season opener on Wednesday against the Golden State Warriors, particularly at power forward. (Jeff Chiu / Associated Press) After five preseason games, the Lakers open their regular season Wednesday at home against the Golden State Warriors. The preseason offered some promising moments, other confounding connections between new teammates and a strong foundation for the new-look team hoping to keep growing through an 82-game season. “You’re always trying to get better,” coach JJ Redick said Friday after the Lakers lost their final preseason game to the Denver Nuggets. “And even later in the season, you tweak plays, you tweak the offense and you tweak coverages. It’s constantly evolving. There’s no, like, ‘oh, we’re done. Now we’re going to go play.’ But we’re ready to go.” Here are five things we learned during the Lakers’ training camp and five preseason games: Ziaire Williams makes his case Lakers forward Ziaire Williams, left, tries to prevent Kings guard Emanuel Sharp from scoring in the lane during a preseason game earlier this month. (Sara Nevis / Associated Press) Ziaire Williams played in only two of the five preseason games, but the 6-foot-9 forward emerged as one of the biggest winners of training camp. The Sierra Canyon High alumnus might go from veteran minimum contract to first-day starter. He was a perfect five-for-five shooting from three-point range during two preseason appearances — both starts — and averaged 13.5 points while taking on a prominent defensive role. During his first two years as the Lakers coach, Redick admired Williams’ intent on the defensive end from afar and commended the forward’s willingness to defend other teams’ star players. And somehow, Williams, then playing for Brooklyn, always seemed to hit shots when he played against the Lakers. Now seeing Williams every day, Redick has come away even more impressed by the 25-year-old’s character and leadership qualities. “Everybody in our building that has been around him for the last, you know, six to eight weeks just recognizes what a special human being he is,” Redick said. “I really believe in him as a player, and I think he’s got a lot of room to grow still, which is exciting for all of us.” While Williams might be the first choice to start at power forward, several contenders had strong preseasons at the position. Jake LaRavia is playing and shooting with confidence again. Sandro Mamukelashvili awed with his versatile offensive game. Adou Thiero showed significant growth from his injury-plagued rookie season. The position remains one of the team’s biggest unknowns, but the preseason could offer some confidence that the Lakers have options. Mamu was breakout star of the preseason Lakers forward Jake LaRavia, left, and Sandro Mamukelashvili try to stop the Kings' Jonathan Mogbo from scoring in a preseason game earlier this month. (Mark J. Terrill / Associated Press) It won’t be long before chants of “Ma-muuuuuuuu” fill Crypto.com Arena. The Georgian forward will quickly become a fan favorite if he continues to provide the all-around offensive game he flashed during the preseason. Mamukelashvili averaged 13.4 points, 4.2 rebounds and 3.4 assists while shooting 55.6% (25 for 45) from the field and 54.2% (13 for 24) from three-point range. Late during the third quarter against Denver, Mamukelashvili dazzled with a three-pointer, a cutting dunk and a defensive rebound that led to an assist to Quentin Grimes for a three-pointer — all in 99 seconds. President of basketball operations Rob Pelinka said before the season that he and Redick wanted to intentionally build a cast of role players who could pass, dribble and shoot. Mamukelashvili checks all the boxes. “Anytime he gets a rebound, we’re encouraging him to push the pace,” guard Austin Reaves said. “He’s a good basketball player, so we’re very excited for what he brings to the team.” How long will rebounding woes linger? Lakers center Walker Kessler, left, powering his way to the basket against two Nuggets defenders, will be the anchor to the team's defense, which will look to improve their rebounding deficiencies. (Ben Liebenberg / Associated Press) Williams scanned the box score in front of him after the Lakers’ preseason finale Friday. He was looking for reassurance about how the Lakers ended the 121-106 loss to the Denver Nuggets. “We did get outrebounded a little bit,” he said, glancing at the Lakers’ 49-44 rebounding deficit. “But not as bad.” The Lakers’ 39.4 rebounds per game ranked second-to-last during the preseason. Defensive rebounds could be a weak point this season for a team still trying to solidify its backup center behind Walker Kessler. Three preseason games without Kessler reinforced to Redick that the Lakers needed to keep two big wings — any combination of Williams, LaRavia, Thiero, Matisse Thybulle or even Doncic, who is a strong rebounder for a guard — on the court to keep pace on the glass. “We can’t just rely on Walker to get 30 rebounds a game,” Williams said of how the team has to approach rebounding. “It’s just not how the game works. So just every person just contributing to it and wanting it more than the other team.” Kessler, standing nearby during Williams’ postgame news conference, poked his head out from behind a black curtain and gave his teammate a thumbs-up. He had 15 rebounds in two games, including 11 defensive boards. The Lakers were outrebounded by one in the two games with Kessler compared with a minus-23 rebounding differential during the first three preseason games. Even the offense needs time Lakers guard Luka Doncic, left, pulls up in the lane for a shot against the Nuggets in the final preseason game Friday. (Ben Liebenberg / Associated Press) Doncic, Reaves and Kessler only played one half together, and Doncic and Reaves only played in the same game twice. During one Laker fastbreak in the first quarter against Denver, while Reaves was taking a steal coast-to-coast for an easy layup, Doncic kept Kessler back on defense and pointed out tactics while they stood in the paint. “There’s going to be some growing pain, just lack of reps together so far,” Reaves said of the chemistry between the team’s new “big three.” “... More than likely going to pick up on it sooner than later. So we’ll continue to grow that over the next couple days and be ready for opening night.” The Lakers averaged 23 turnovers per game during the preseason. Guard Collin Sexton’s absence because of a lower leg injury showed up in the Lakers’ turnover struggles. Even two of the premier guards in the league won’t be enough to handle all of the Lakers’ ball-handling, especially if Bronny James continues to struggle as he did during the preseason. James, after working into the injury-laden postseason rotation last year, averaged just 16.4 minutes per preseason game with 2.2 points per game on one-for-eight shooting from three. He had 12 rebounds, 14 assists and 12 turnovers during the five games. The roster isn’t done changing The Lakers have to cut their roster to 15 by the opener. Pelinka mentioned the possibility of consolidation trades to reach the maximum number, but no transactions have materialized, especially with the Lakers trying to cling to their limited draft assets. They don’t control their own first-round pick until 2032 and don’t have a second-round selection until 2031. If the Lakers can’t pull off a deal, forward Dalton Knecht could be at risk of being waived. Since getting traded as a rookie and returning when the transaction was rescinded, the 17th overall pick in the 2024 draft has never carved out a steady role with the Lakers. Early, he looked like he could be the steal of the draft when he averaged 18.9 points per game during a nine-game stretch in November 2024, including a two-game, 64-point heater in which he hit 14 of 24 three-pointers. He scored more points in his 19 NBA games (231) than he did all of last season (228). “I think the biggest thing is the team changed,” Redick said before Friday’s game of Knecht’s career arc. “The team changed. The needs changed, the fit changed. I think he got better as a player over the last two years. I think each guy has, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the amount of injuries we had. So I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings and he’s in a tough spot right now.” Forward Jarred Vanderbilt, who has about $25 million left on his contract over the next two seasons, did not suit up for Friday’s preseason finale. After joining the team through a trade from Washington this offseason, guard Jaden Hardy understood that roster moves would continue through training camp. On the fringe of the rotation, he said he didn’t let it bother him. “I just came in [with a] clear head, clear mind, new situation, new opportunity,” said Hardy, who has a $6-million salary this season and a team option for next year. “I feel like it’s a blessing to be here and I’m just coming in here every day working, taking care of my business.” He stated his case for a roster spot with 13 points in 14 minutes Friday. stories.title: SB Nation Reacts: Turn off the injury option
stories.summary: Our deepest fear is not that we are inadequate. Our deepest fear is that we are injured beyond measure. It is our availability, not our ability, that most frightens us.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS , MN - APRIL 25: Rudy Gobert (27), Anthony Edwards (5), Julius Randle (30), and Jaden McDaniels (3) of the Minnesota Timberwolves call for a stoppage in action after Donte DiVincenzo (0) went down with an apparent injury during the first quarter of game four of their NBA Playoffs series against the Denver Nuggets at the Target Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota on Saturday, April 25, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images As the season is just days away from kicking off, we asked you all for the last time. Your answer? “Our deepest fear is not that we are inadequate. Our deepest fear is that we are injured beyond measure. It is our availability, not our ability, that most frightens us. Your playing dinged up does not serve the world. There is nothing enlightened about playing through ailments so that other teams won’t feel secure in their playoff seeing. We are all meant to load manage as Kawhi Leonard does. It’s not just in some of us; it is in everyone. And as we let our own rest shine, we unconsciously give other people permission to do the same. As we are liberated from our own fear, our presence automatically liberates others.” To be fair, most teams likely fear the same thing. Injuries are the great equalizer, or more like “un-equalizer.” Wolves fans are no strangers to this, as we saw just how much it impacted their 2026 postseason run. Having a fully healthy Anthony Edwards, let alone an available Donte DiVincenzo, could have made a huge difference in the 2-4 series loss to the San Antonio Spurs . Some of you in the comments section specifically referenced the concern of injury to Rudy Gobert. It falls in line with the frontcourt depth concern, as his only true backup is a 19-year-old athletic freak who only started playing basketball around when Anthony Edwards was drafted by Minnesota. The only other realistic options behind him would be Trey Lyles or two-player Rocco Zikarsky. Is 38-year-old Kevin Love kicking open the door to try and help his case to get his jersey retired after Kevin Garnett? Interestingly enough, another high vote went towards “Winning too many games.” I added that as a sort of joke response, but it is reasonable to be concerned about a team that “ replaced moodiness with giddiness ” to take things seriously enough. I can already see the media running with a story like: Anthony Edwards spotted laughing while hopping in LaMelo Ball’s Hummer (which a personal driver is at the wheel of) after a four-point loss against the Memphis Grizzlies in March because they’re currently second in the Western Conference. If you’re into sports betting stuff (I am not), FanDuel has the Timberwolves at +1400 odds to win the Western Conference . They certainly don’t have the concern of the Wolves “winning too much.” Weird, considering Minnesota is most certainly going 82-0.

stories.title: Ziaire Williams emerges as fan-favorite for Lakers’ fifth starter
stories.summary: Lakers fans have spoken, and they want Williams to fill the fifth spot in the starting lineup.
stories.detailText: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NBA. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Lakers fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. The Los Angeles Lakers’ preseason officially came to a close with their 121-106 loss to the Denver Nuggets , and we still don’t have a concrete answer on what their opening-night starting lineup will be. But the fans have a preference. We’ve drawn a general conclusion that Quentin Grimes would be joining Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler in the starting lineup, considering that he started four of the five games in the preseason. However, the final spot in the lineup has mostly been up for grabs. For this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey , we asked fans who they think should slot in next to the four above between Ziaire Williams, Jake LaRavia, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Matisse Thybulle, each of whom has made strong cases through the whirlwind of lineups we’ve seen all preseason. And there was a clear winner. JJ Redick may have given the final stamp of approval based on the five he started with in their preseason finale on Friday. Williams joined Dončić, Reaves, Kessler, and Thybulle against the Nuggets, something Redick said he wanted to try, especially with Grimes on the bench. Williams’ 6-foot-9 frame and 3-and-D ability make him the most ideal candidate to fill the position. In the two preseason games he played, he averaged 13.5 points in 15.6 minutes per game and made all five 3-pointers he attempted. Williams has never actualized his perimeter shooting potential, registering below-average overall 3-point shot quality with Brooklyn last season. But he is already getting better looks playing with two of the league’s best offensive creators. “Man, my life is definitely easier, to say the least,” Williams said after Friday’s loss. “Just playing with high-level playmakers, guys who know how to win and, you know, guys who’ve been in the league for a long time. I just know my role, and I feel like I just couldn’t be in a better situation.” An overwhelming 44% of Lakers fans seem aligned with Redick in their preference for Williams to start. His skillset complements the other four projected starters. Now it’s up to him to continue the production he’s put out in his short preseason stints and help raise the ceiling of the Lakers as contenders . You can follow Connor on Twitter at @cmorenoNBA .

stories.title: Roundtable: Who will be the NBA MVP this season?
stories.summary: Is this the year Luka or Wemby break through?
stories.detailText: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 15: A detailed view of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander #2 of the Oklahoma City Thunder jersey during the game against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center on October 15, 2026 in Houston, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images The staff question this week was about the NBA vs just the Mavericks: who is going to be the NBA’s MVP this year? David : I’m going with Luka Doncic. He is primed for the breakthrough MVP award that we thought he’d get three seasons ago. His numbers this year will be ridiculous; like 35 points, 10 rebounds, and nine assists kind of ridiculous. The Lakers will win 50 games, and the media will finally come around to him now that his sleek figure fits their narrative. It’s too early for Wemby, too absurd for an SGA three-peat, and too much Luka for anyone else. Salvador : I would go 50/50 between Wemby and Luka. If Wemby qualifies, I think he wins it as voters tend to reward players from the year before (their playoff run), but I agree for the most part with David Michael : The MVP award is an almost impossible task. There are always three or four players worthy of the award, and somehow it seems to be decided by things that didn’t necessarily take place during the regular season. The race is often so tight that a few playoff games enter the equation, or a player from last year’s championship team gets the nod, etc. As objective as I can be, I’ll go with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. I do think he will be hard-pressed to convince voters to give him a third straight, especially after a loss in the Western Conference Finals last season, but I suspect the Thunder are going to be one of the league’s best teams and he’s at a stage in his career where he may just have yet another level to attain. Victor Wembanyama is also highly likely to get the award based on betting odds, but I think enough voters will be hesitant to give it to a third-year player that it will cost him the honor. I suspect he would have to leave no doubt while the Spurs were the #1 seed by a decent margin for him to get it, and I think the Thunder will have something to say about that. So, factoring in voter bias, I suspect both players will be in a tight race, with SGA winning it behind a Thunder team that lands ahead of the Spurs in the standings. Bryan : My pick for MVP of the 2026-2027 season is…the Toronto Raptors’ own Scottie Barnes. The Knicks, Celtics, Raptors, Pacers, Sixers, Heat and Pistons are all going to be in a race for the number one seed in the East, and if it isn’t the Knicks or Celtics who grab it, the Raptors have as good a chance as anyone. Kawhi Leonard will not get a serious look as MVP for obvious reasons, but Scottie had a coming-out party in last year’s playoffs and announced himself as one of the 12 to 17 best players in the league. As someone sharing the primary shot creation burden with Kawhi and the most important defender on what should compete with Boston, OKC, and San Antonio for the best defense in the league, Barnes will have plenty of narrative tailwind propelling him forward as long as the voters are paying attention. While the splash of the Kawhi acquisition should draw national media eyeballs, hopefully the play of their emerging star will keep them watching. Honorable mentions to Jayson Tatum and Tyrese Haliburton, but I’d rather not lay those expectations on guys still in their first full year back from Achilles injuries. Matt: It feels like it would take an act of God for Wemby not to win it. The Spurs are set to run back probably the best roster in the NBA after a Finals run that was arguably ahead of schedule. And the powers that be in the NBA seem to love a linear, uncomplicated narrative. Wemby has done all of the necessary steps thus far to be in consideration. If he stays healthy, going from rookie phenom to DPOY to team leader of a Finals runner-up, all the pieces have aligned for Wemby to be anointed so long as nothing catastrophic befalls San Antonio. Tyler : Okay, now that I’ve collected myself from reading Bryan’s prediction, let’s get nuts. Anthony Edwards is your 2026-27 NBA MVP. Why? Well, the addition of Lamelo Ball gets him out of the square peg, round hole situation he was in last season when he was running point. Because of that, he’ll get to launch more wide open threes generated by Ball. By the way, Edwards was 40% from deep on 8.4 attempts last year, after being 39.5% on over 10 attempts per game previously. Beyond that, Edwards was near 50% on catch and shoot looks. Guess who all of a sudden will get a ton of catch and shoot looks? The man can shoot, the man can defend, and he’s one of the three most likable players in the entire NBA. If Minnesota is a top three seed, that is your MVP.

stories.title: James, Embiid play 76ers' preseason finale, 'still working on our rhythm'
stories.summary: Without VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday night's 125-120 loss to the Celtics, 76ers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season, including LeBron James and Joel Embiid playing preseason highs in minutes.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- As the 76ers begin a season with a star-laden roster, center Joel Embiid rejects the narrative that anyone needs to sacrifice for this team to succeed. "I'm against the concept of sacrificing," Embiid said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat." Albeit without second-year starting guard VJ Edgecombe , who was held out of Friday's 125-120 loss to the Boston Celtics for precautionary reasons, Sixers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season. The other active Sixers starters -- LeBron James , Tyrese Maxey , Jaylen Brown and Embiid -- all played preseason highs in minutes and well into the second half. Embiid, who struggled in his last appearance two games ago against the Brooklyn Nets , finishing with six points and eight turnovers, was dominant.​ He scored 27 points, grabbed eight rebounds and added five assists. In the third quarter, he had one of the game's highlights when he threw down an emphatic dunk that drew roars from fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena. "It's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again," Embiid said with a smile. "I guess I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed." Still, the group never looked comfortable together on the floor, despite playing against Celtics reserves. After the game, players didn't shy away from their somewhat disjointed performance. Brown pointed to the team's spacing Friday night, which he said led to turnovers, as one of the many things they need to fix moving forward. "We're not where we want to be yet," he said. "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day." James echoed Brown's comments, but neither seemed concerned about the Sixers' ability to eventually jell. "We're getting there," James said. "I mean, obviously we are a couple of weeks in, so we're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks, and it's not going to be perfect." The Sixers open the regular season against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.

stories.title: No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa exits Wizards' preseason game with ankle injury
stories.summary: Washington Wizards' AJ Dybantsa appeared to injure his ankle Friday against the Pelicans, but the extent of the injury has not been disclosed.
stories.detailText: No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, AJ Dybantsa , was forced to leave the Washington Wizards ' preseason matchup Friday, Oct. 16, against the New Orleans Pelicans after suffering an apparent ankle injury. The injury happened when Dybantsa attempted a midrange jump shot and landed awkwardly on his ankle, causing him to collapse to the court in visible pain as he grabbed his ankle. He managed to get up and limped off to the locker room for further examination. Prior to his exit, Dybantsa put up 12 points in just 15 minutes. Ultimately, the Wizards narrowly lost to the Pelicans, 107-106. Wizards head coach Brian Keefe told reporters after the game that Dybantsa had sustained a mild ankle sprain and was taken out of the game as a precautionary measure. As of Saturday morning, no further update had been provided on the extent of the injury. "We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said on Friday. The Wizards now face a wait-and-see approach to see if Dybantsa will be available for their regular-season opener, which is just four days away. Washington is set to host the Milwaukee Bucks at Capital One Arena on Wednesday, Oct. 21, with tipoff scheduled for 7 p.m. ET. teamStories.summary: The Spurs will start guards De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper alongside Devin Vassell and Victor Wembanyama when they face the Thunder in Tuesday's season opener.
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO -- Spurs coach Mitch Johnson on Friday squashed any suspense going into the season by announcing his three-guard lineup will start in Tuesday's opener against the Thunder . "We're planning on starting that same crew [in the opener]," Johnson said. San Antonio first deployed its three-guard starting lineup of De'Aaron Fox , Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper , alongside Devin Vassell and Victor Wembanyama , in a preseason win over the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday, when the Spurs finished at plus-10 in the trio's 11 minutes together on the floor. The Suns rested most of their rotation players in that outing, which started with the Spurs shooting 1-for-10 from the floor. The Spurs shot 2-for-9 on 3-pointers when Fox, Castle and Harper shared the floor against the Suns, with Vassell and Wembanyama combining to miss all six of their 3-point attempts. Despite a size disadvantage, the Spurs won the rebounding battle 13-11 when the trio played. "When it clicked, it clicked," Wembanyama said. "The biggest thing is I've got handlers all around me, guys we want to put the ball in their hands and pick and roll around me." Wembanyama finished with the most total touches (24) while playing with the three guards. Wembanyama brought the ball up the floor for five possessions, second most when sharing the court with the trio. Fox, Castle, and Harper played 69 minutes together last season, including 25 in the NBA Finals, with Spurs opponents outscoring them by 47 points in those minutes. The Spurs finished with a plus-9.4 net rating when just Fox and Castle shared the floor in the regular season, plus-6.2 with Fox and Harper and plus-11.0 with Harper and Castle. Despite last season's small sample size, Johnson said he wanted to lean into the idea this season of starting games with the club's five best players instead of having one come off the bench. "We have a talented group, especially in the backcourt," Fox said. "When we're making shots, it allows other guys to be able to get downhill. We can spread the defense out, and teams know what we want to do. There's no secret about it. So a lot of our season, a lot of how special that first group can be, it's going to be predicated on how we shoot the ball." Fox, Castle and Harper shot a combined 9-for-21 from the field in Wednesday's win over the Suns and 3-for-6 from 3-point range. The trio contributed 19 points Friday in the first quarter against the Sacramento Kings as the Spurs stormed to a 42-18 lead. "We have guys that can create for themselves and create for others," Fox said. "So we try to generate the easiest shot possible." Information from ESPN Research was used in this report.

teamStories.title: Open Thread: How age impacts ever-changing landscape of the NBA
teamStories.summary: Today’s game has the largest swath of young players
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - NOVEMBER 15: LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers speaks with Stephon Castle #5 of the San Antonio Spurs after the NBA Cup game on NOVEMBER 15, 2024 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2024 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images San Antonio Spurs former vice president for strategic research Kirk Goldsberry recently posted this graphic. View this post on Instagram “ It’s a young man’s game, and increasingly so. Over 80% of the NBA is now 29 or younger. This hasn’t always been the case but the combination of pace and space basketball with the lack of durability we associate with older players has resulted in the NBA getting younger and younger. Pretty soon it’s just gonna be 50 year-old LeBron and 500 23 year-olds! ” Goldsberry is an expert of the modern game, differentiating how the game has evolved. In addition to his time with the Spurs, he wrote for Grantland , the ESPN blog brainchild of Bill Simmons, from 2012-2015. Other notable writings include The Kobe Assist , The Evolution of King James , and DataBall . His 2019 book SprawlBall: A Visual Tour of the New Era of the NBA commented on the inefficiency of shots taken from the restricted area to the three-point line. While the game has skewed younger, Goldsberry doesn’t delve into the rationale for the shift. Is it the pace of the game wearing players out at an earlier age? It’s commonly accepted that load management and modern healthcare allows for players to have longer careers. So why are they not? Perhaps the propensity to draft and sign younger players feeds into the “win now” mentality that franchises have established. It pairs with the hiring and firing of coaches without allowing time for a team to fully develop. Whatever the reason, players are entering the league younger — the “one and done” collegiate effect — and exiting the league sooner. Think of former Spurs shooting guard Lonnie Walker IV. At age 27, he’s played on four teams over seven seasons. Now, at age 27, it looks as if his time in the NBA is over. He can still have a long and prosperous career overseas (in fact, he just signed with Beşiktaş of the Turkish Basketbol Süper Ligi two days ago). Seven years seems to a fair amount of time to analyze a player’s NBA career. But is it his age relevant to his ability to play in the NBA, or is he being assessed solely on talent? A look at many players could yield a clearer picture. For now, it’s important to note that players do not have the time to develop that they did a quarter century ago. Welcome to the Thread. Join in the conversation, start your own discussion, and share your thoughts. This is the Spurs community, your Spurs community. Thanks for being here. Our community guidelines apply which should remind everyone to be cool, avoid personal attacks, not to troll and to watch the language.

stories.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts on IR due to blood clot, expected to be out indefinitely
stories.summary: The Eagles have decided to place Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after consultations with numerous doctors and experts, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
stories.detailText: The Philadelphia Eagles have decided to place Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after consultations with numerous doctors and experts that continued into Saturday, sources told ESPN and NFL Network. The move will sideline the star quarterback indefinitely, according to sources. The Eagles, who officially announced the move Saturday afternoon, were waiting to make a roster decision until after consulting with medical experts, according to sources. Ever since Hurts started dealing with the superficial blood clot in his calf, the Eagles have been attempting to explore every option and gather as much information as possible. Hurts has met with doctors and had others review his blood clot and weigh in with their knowledge. At some time over the past 24 hours, additional information surfaced that made Philadelphia believe the wisest course of action was to place Hurts on IR, giving him the time he needs to heal. The Eagles maintained all along that they weren't going to rush into any decisions about Hurts' future, which is why they waited until Thursday to rule out the three-time Pro Bowler for Sunday's home game against the Carolina Panthers . Hurts now will miss games against the Panthers, Dallas Cowboys , Washington Commanders and New York Giants before the Eagles have their bye in Week 10 with a chance to fully evaluate their quarterback's health and their team's outlook. Philadelphia believes the blood clot is treatable, and the ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, with the Eagles ready to follow his lead. In most cases, blood clots are treated with anticoagulants, otherwise known as blood thinners. A player cannot play while on blood thinners. In general, the minimum time frame for a moderate dose of anticoagulants is six weeks, sources said. There is a possibility, if the clot is minor enough, that doctors begin with anti-inflammatories only, while continuing to monitor. If the clot were to move, as the team said happened in Hurts' case, blood thinners are often the answer. If the clot were to worsen, blood thinners for roughly three months would be the next course of action. Some doctors around the NFL who have not examined Hurts believe the blood clot could sideline him several weeks. One team's doctor texted ESPN: "It is a broad range and nuance based on size and location and hematology evaluation, but could be six weeks." Another team's doctor had a similar estimation. The Eagles released a lengthy statement Thursday detailing the process that led to the discovery of the blood clot and to Hurts being ruled out for Sunday's game. While Hurts has been receiving treatment, the Eagles have been working to fortify their roster. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers, and rookie Cole Payton was promoted to backup. Philadelphia also signed quarterback Joe Milton off Dallas' practice squad. By NFL rules, Milton must be on the Eagles' roster for three weeks. This is just the latest sequence in what has been a chaotic stretch for the organization that has included hamstring injuries to running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith , the retirement of future Hall of Fame offensive tackle Lane Johnson and the trade of Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens . Amid the injuries and turnover on their offensive line, the Eagles have gotten off to a rough start offensively this season. They enter Sunday in the bottom five in the NFL in points per game (18.4, 29th), total yards per game (262.2, 31st), yards per play (4.5, 30th) and passing yards per game (170.6, 28th). The Eagles have failed to score 25 points in seven consecutive regular-season games, their longest such streak since Nick Sirianni became their coach before the 2021 season. Philadelphia has gone three-and-out on 38% of its possessions, the highest in the NFL this season. The Eagles' offense has struggled to stay on the field, specifically in the second half, going three-and-out on 52% of its second-half possessions, which is on pace to be the highest by any NFL team in the past 20 seasons. Philadelphia has been outgained by a league-leading 115 yards per game in the second half this season; the next-worst team in that category is the Indianapolis Colts , who have been outgained by 38 yards per game in the second half.

The Packers are dealing with several injuries, which led to four players being ruled out on Friday , forcing Green Bay to push up some reinforcements. stories.title: Cowboys need to approach the next two games as must wins
stories.summary: The next two weeks are huge for the Cowboys.
stories.detailText: Amanda McCoy/Fort Worth Star-Telegram/Tribune News Service via Getty Images There are currently some very frustrating vibes surrounding the Dallas Cowboys. Through the first fives games, they’ve alternated wins and losses, which is the epitome of an average football team. When they lost to the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, it wasn’t that they didn’t win, it was how poorly they looked while doing it. Their defense made undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels look like a seasoned pro, and their offense, which is usually what they can fall back on, scored just 16 points. It’s been a display of inconsistency by the Cowboys so far this season. One thing that’s in their favor in terms of having a shot at the playoffs is that the NFC East, or NFC Least as its been nicknamed, is still more than winnable. The New York Giants lead the division at 3-1-1. Behind them are the Philadelphia Eagles and the Cowboys at 2-3, and the Washington Commanders are 1-3-1. Dallas has the Green Bay Packers on their slate for Sunday Night Football in Week 6 followed by the Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 7. These games are very important of course, but the Cowboys need to approach these as must wins. As much as the Cowboys could win the next two games, their up and down play could easily lead to back-to-back losses as well. They would fall to 2-5 if that was the case, and put them in a very bad spot not even half way through the season. It would not only result in them being 1-2 in division play, but that would give them four losses in the NFC, which would be crippling when it comes to tie breakers for a potential playoff spot. Since the playoff extension in 1990, 155 teams have started the season with a 2-5 record. Only nine of those teams have made the postseason, which is 5.81%. It’s just a very deep hole to dig out of and the Cowboys still have teams like the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and Jacksonville Jaguars on their schedule. Those teams have the flaws as well, but they’ll also be extremely difficult to beat. The Cowboys need to adopt a back against the wall mentality going forward and stack up some wins quickly. After the Packers and the Eagles, they will face the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals and the 2-3 Indianapolis Colts. So, if they can pull out victories over the next few weeks, they have a shot to go on a nice run and climb up the standings in the NFC significantly. Do you think the Cowboys can knock off the Packers and the Eagles in the next two games? Let us know your thoughts and prediction in the comments.

stories.title: Lions’ DJ Wonnum latest to receive fine that could lead to suspension
stories.summary: Lions defensive end DJ Wonnum could face a suspension if he commits two more penalties.
stories.detailText: Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) reacts after a play against Detroit Lions defensive end DJ Wonnum (98) during the second quarter at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last week, Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell received a $15,930 fine for a hip- drop tackle against the Carolina Panthers. This week, it was DJ Wonnum who was fined for the same infraction, costing him $12,611 out of his paycheck. As we explained in the story about Campbell’s penalty, there’s more concern than just a fine for players who committed a hip-drop tackle. A hip-drop tackle is one of five fouls that are considered “major,” and would result in a one-game fine if repeated a total of three times, per an NFL rule that was implemented this year. The other fouls that fall under this category are horse collar tackle, launching, hit on a defenseless player, and a blindside block. Here’s the wording of the new NFL rule . Players who commit three offenses in any of these categories during a season will be suspended for one game. Players who commit only one violation will receive 50 percent of their fine back at the end of the season. As for the hip-drop tackle, here’s video of Wonnum’s penalty, which is clearly a foul: Here’s video of Lions defensive end DJ Wonnum’s hip drop tackle that resulted in a $ 12,611 fine. pic.twitter.com/VQrb0HwHDP — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) October 17, 2026 The three parts to a hip-drop tackle are: grab the runner with both hands, unweights by swiveling their body around, then landing on the player’s legs below the knee. Wonnum clearly does all three of those things to Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. But like the Campbell foul last week, there was no penalty flag throw on the play live. No other Lions players were fined for the Cardinals game, but Cardinals running back Elijah Higgins was fined $20,411 for the use of his helmet.

stories.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts placed on IR, will miss the Week 9 Giants game
stories.summary: The Eagles will be without QB Jalen Hurts when they play the NY Giants in Week 9
stories.detailText: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Eagles have placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on the injured reserve. Hurts will now be out for the next four weeks, and his earliest possible return is after the New York Giants travel to Philly to take on the Eagles in Week 9. While Hurts will be eligible to return following the Eagles’ Week 11 bye, Adam Schefter reports that Hurts is considered sidelined indefinitely. The move is in response to the blood clot which has become an increasing concern for both Hurts and the Eagles. The blood clot was originally caused when he was cleated earlier in the season and he played through the injury in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . However, tests have since shown that the clot has moved, sparking significant concern. ESPN is reporting that Hurts could be treated with blood thinners, and the average treatment course being six weeks. However, it’s possible that he could be sidelined for as long as three months, which would effectively be season-ending. The Eagles are tied with the Dallas Cowboys at 2-3 on the season, and 1.5 games behind the first place Giants. Philly’s season started as disappointing before quickly spiraling after the retirement of RT Lane Johnson , injuries to RB Saquon Barkley and WR DeVonta Smith , and the trade of OC Cam Jurgens . The loss of Hurts is yet another significant blow to the Eagles’ season. The Giants will have their own bye week in Week 8, and will play the Eagles immediately after in Week 9. That game is followed by a home game against the Washington Commanders in Week 10 on Thursday Night Football. Nobody wants to see an opponent deal with injury, particularly something as potentially serious as a blood clot. However, this turn of events is another opportunity for the Giants to extend their lead over the Eagles in the division.

Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday. Impact: Garrett Wilson is in line to see all the volume he can handle. Kenyon Sadiq - TE (concussion) Sadiq played through a back injury in Week 5 before suffering a concussion. Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that the team would activate Dell's 21-day practice window this week. He was limited on Wednesday but ruled out for Week 5 Friday.
