Impact: Expect Jaylin Noel to serve as the primary slot receiver while newcomer Kayshon Boutte starts on the perimeter opposite Nico Collins , for the time being. Dell could work his way back into primary slot duties once healthy. The Texans acquired former first-round wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. following their Week 5 win over the Titans. If Dell travels, he could play, though he offers no floor. David Montgomery - RB (groin) Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Montgomery is " week-to-week " with a groin injury. He was ruled out for Week 6 Friday. Impact: The expected multi-game absence leaves Woody Marks alone atop the backfield depth chart, in a role that has yielded but on fantasy-relevant box score through the season's first five weeks. Even so, fantasy managers in a bind can prioritize Marks off waivers ahead of another difficult matchup against the Jaguars in London. Jayden Higgins - WR (knee) Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp. Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury ◆ Indianapolis Colts Josh Downs - WR (rest/hamstring) Downs was limited on Wednesday and was removed from the injury report Friday . Impact: Rest-associated designations can typically be ignored, but the Colts kept a "rest/groin" designation next to Keenan Allen's name recently, before ruling him out at the end of the week. We expect Downs to play, but his progress must be monitored. Daniel Jones - QB (ankle) Jones is practicing in full and should be expected to play in Week 6 . Impact: Jones is still regaining his push-off strength from last year's Achilles tendon rupture. Adding an ankle injury is not ideal. He is a QB2. Alec Pierce - WR (heel) Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Impact: Josh Downs should serve as the primary option through the air for as long as Pierce remains sidelined. The team signed veteran field-stretcher Darius Slayton in the wake of Pierce's injury, although he is unlikely to return weekly fantasy production. Slayton (knee) was ruled out for Week 5 on Friday. Tyler Warren - TE (groin) Warren was added to the team's injury report Friday and was designated questionable for Week 6 against the Titans. Impact: Warren's late addition to the injury report spells trouble for his potential availability against the Titans. An absence would leave the Colts without one of their top play makers, potentially filtering additional volume to Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs . ◆ Jacksonville Jaguars The Jaguars emerged from their Week 5 win over the Eagles absent any fantasy-relevant injuries. ◆ Tennessee Titans Tyjae Spears - RB (knee) Spears remains limited in practice as usual . He is questionable for Week 6. Impact: None. AFC West ◆ Denver Broncos Pat Bryant - WR (ankle) Bryant suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 4 loss to the 49ers and is reportedly expected to miss "a few weeks." He was placed on injured reserve Friday. Impact: Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims appear to be the next men up in Bryant's absence, although the team could use a "sum of all parts" mentality to bridge his absence, considering historical trends. Alpha wide receiver Jaylen Waddle would be the primary beneficiary. Jonah Coleman - RB (ankle) The team shocked fantasy managers Saturday, sending him to short-term injured reserve . He will be eligible to return in mid-October. Impact: Coleman was initially viewed as the potential Week 3 starter, given Harvey and Dobbins' ailments. Dobbins and Harvey will revert to a backfield tandem in the rookie's absence. Jaylen Waddle - WR (shoulder) Waddle suffered a shoulder injury on Thursday Night Football, briefly departing the contest before returning to finish the game. Impact: Fantasy managers will want to track the veteran receiver's status in the coming week. ◆ Kansas City Chiefs Rashee Rice - WR (hamstring) Rice departed Week 4 with a hamstring injury and is reportedly looking at a multi-week absence. He was sidelined to begin Week 6 and was ruled out Friday. Impact: It was Jalen Royals who stepped into Rice's role following the latter's departure, although rookie Cyrus Allen would appear to be a better fit in the short term. The Chiefs are now without a viable deep threat following the devastating injury suffered by Tyquan Thornton, with reports surfacing that they have reached out to free agent Tyreek Hill . Stay tuned as this saga unfolds. Tyquan Thornton - WR (ankle) Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks. Impact: See above. ◆ Las Vegas Raiders Brock Bowers - TE (knee) The Raiders continue to give Bowers half-days on Wednesday . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Bills. Impact: None. He is the overall TE1. Ashton Jeanty - RB (foot/ankle) Head coach Klint Kubiak said Jeanty is starting to " feel a lot better ." Jeanty is practicing in full for Week 6 and was removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: Jeanty is clearly limited by the injuries, ceding touches to Mike Washington and Dylan Laube . For now, he is a borderline RB1/2. Jalen Nailor - WR (concussion) Nailor was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 6. Impact: Likely none. Dont’e Thornton - WR (hamstring) Thornton is reportedly "getting close" but was ruled out for Week 6 Friday. Impact: Thornton could carve out a role as a deep threat, once healthy, but can only be viewed as a dart throw. Jack Bech - WR (forearm) The Raiders placed Bech on injured reserve in Week 4. Impact : Raiders wide receiver Tre Tucker could line up in the slot more often. ◆ Los Angeles Chargers Ladd McConkey - WR ( foot ) McConkey, Quentin Johnston (chest), KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad) and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) were limited. Tre' Harris (hamstring) did not practice. The team removed McConkey and Johnston from the injury report Friday , while Lambert-Smith and Brenen Thompson are listed as questionable. Harris was ruled out for Week 6. Impact: McConkey is the only Chargers wide receiver who should definitely be in re-draft lineups against the Chiefs in Week 6. Quentin Johnston - WR (chest) See above . Impact: See above. David Njoku - TE (fibula) Njoku is looking at an extended absence after being carted from the field in the team's Week 2 loss to the Raiders. The Chargers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . Impact: See above. NFC East ◆ Dallas Cowboys Malik Davis - RB (hip) Davis was placed on injured reserve and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Impact: The Cowboys released both Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah at roster cuts and now have only Emari Demercado on the active roster behind starter Javonte Williams . Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1 in Week 2. CeeDee Lamb - WR (quad) Lamb departed the team's Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. He is practicing in full for Week 6 . Impact: None. ◆ New York Giants Isaiah Likely - TE (foot) Likely is practicing in full for Week 6 . Impact: None. Darnell Mooney - WR (neck) Mooney was limited on Wednesday . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Saints in Week 6. Impact: None. Jaxson Dart - QB (knee) Dart injured his MCL, PCL and meniscus on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football against the Rams. He will undergo surgery to address the MCL and meniscus and miss the rest of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is possible for Dart to return in the postseason, although this is unlikely. Impact: Backup Jameis Winston was largely unable to sustain drives following Dart's departure. Dart's absence has an adverse effect on all skill position players in New York, most notably Malik Nabers , Isaiah Likely , and Cam Skattebo . We'll know more regarding Dart's expected timeline later this week. ◆ Philadelphia Eagles Saquon Barkley - RB (hamstring) The veteran workhorse pulled up lame in the second quarter of Week 4 and is reportedly considered "week-to-week." He did not play in Week 5 but the team is reportedly " hopeful " to get back their franchise back for Week 6. He was ruled out for Week 6 Friday. Impact: Primary backup Tank Bigsby also departed the team's Week 4 loss to the Rams, leaving with a core muscle injury that requires surgery. He was placed on injured reserve Monday. Running back Will Shipley the suffered an injury in Week 5. The Philadelphia backfield is currently a mess. Jalen Hurts - QB (blood clot) Team doctors discovered a blood clot in Hurts' calf. He was ruled out for Week 6 and could be looking at an extended absence. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday. Impact: Hurts is currently sidelined indefinitely. Tanner McKee enters the starting lineup under center following the release of Andy Dalton. The Philadelphia offense could be in trouble in the immediate future considering the sheer number of injuries. Tank Bigsby - RB (core) See above. Impact: See above. Will Shipley - RB (foot) Shipley reportedly suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot in Week 5. He is expected to miss multiple weeks. Impact: Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele are the only healthy backs currently on the roster, assuming Saquon Barkley misses another week. Neither are overly exciting streaming options, although we would prioritize Pierce. DeVonta Smith - WR (hamstring/toe) Smith did not practice on Wednesday after playing through his hamstring injury in Week 3. He missed Weeks 4-5, and remains sidelined to begin Week 6. He is now also listed with a toe injury . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Panthers. Impact: Smith's hamstring was an issue in training camp. He returns to an offense without both Saquon Barkley and Jalen Hurts, also missing three starting offensive linemen. Regardless, Smith can be started as a viable WR2 as the primary option through the air. Dontayvion Wicks - WR (hamstring) Wicks was limited to begin Week 6. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will face the Panthers. Impact: Wicks played through the injury last week. He remains a shaky FLEX. Eli Stowers - TE (hamstring/quad) The Eagles placed Stowers on injured reserve . He was limited to begin Week 6, but does not need to be rostered . Impact: Stowers appears unlikely to have a meaningful role in the offense during his rookie season. ◆ Washington Commanders Terry McLaurin - WR (hamstring) McLaurin remains sidelined in Week 5 after injuring his hamstring during a Week 4 practice . He played in Week 5 after being a true game-time decision and was removed from the injury report Saturday. Impact: Fantasy managers will want to track his status in the coming days to ensure he did not suffer a setback. Stefon Diggs - WR (hamstring) Diggs apparently injured his hamstring in Week 4 and remains sidelined to begin Week 5 . He was ruled out for Week 5 Friday and listed as questionable for Week 6. Impact: Diggs could return following a one-game absence. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Commanders play on Monday Night Football in Week 6. Marcus Mariota - QB (knee) Mariota departed the team's Week 4 loss in London with a sprained MCL , leaving Athan Kaliakmanis as the likely backup, for the time being. Mariota remained sidelined in Week 5 and was ruled out for Week 6. Impact: None. Jaylin Lane - WR (ankle) Lane suffered a dislocated ankle and fracture in Week 4 and is likely done for the season. Impact: Minimal. Lane was primarily a special teams contributor. Jacory Croskey-Merritt - RB (groin) Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice this week and ruled out for Week 6 against the 49ers. Impact: Expect Rachaad White to fill in as the primary rusher, with Austin Ekeler on hand to soak up primary change of pace duties. White can be started as a viable FLEX option while Ekeler is likely best left on fantasy benches. NFC North ◆ Chicago Bears Caleb Williams - QB (hamstring) Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain in the team's Week 2 loss to the Vikings. He is practicing in full for Week 6. Although listed as questionable, Williams posted a video to social media Friday hinting at a likely return. Impact: Williams' expected return comes on the heels of a seven-point, five-turnover outing against the division rival Packers with a combination of Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum under center. Williams will be a back-end QB1 against the pass-funnel Falcons in Week 6. Kyle Monangai - RB (thumb/toe) Head coach Ben Johnson labeled Monangai as " day-to-day " with a thumb injury suffered in Week 4. Johnson said Monangai's thumb injury is not an " issue ," but did not address the toe injury. Monangai was ultimately ruled out for Week 5. He remains sidelined and was ruled out for Week 6. Impact: D'Andre Swift suddenly finds himself in one of the better spots for Week 5, with the backfield mostly to himself for as long as Monangai remains sidelined. Roschon Johnson is likely to be involved, but not to the extent that Monangai would have been. Fire up Swift in all formats as a middling RB1 in a difficult matchup against the Falcons, should Monangai miss another week. ◆ Detroit Lions Isiah Pacheco - RB (back) Pacheco was placed on injured reserve to start the season. General Manager Brad Holmes said he "hopes Pacheco returns this season." Impact: Well, that doesn't sound great. There appears to be something more insidious going on with Pacheco's back than initially thought. Lions coach Dan Campbell said running backs Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could split touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs . Saylors appears to be the first player up. Gibbs handled an absurd 34 opportunities, of 37 total running back opportunities, in the team's Week 1, overtime win over the Saints ◆ Green Bay Packers Josh Jacobs - RB (commissioner exempt list) Jacobs is set to be removed from the commissioner exempt list Monday and is in line to return to the team for Week 7. Impact: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports the league investigation will continue and the veteran back could face additional punitive actions should they eventually view the footage of the incident. For now, Jacobs returns as an unquestioned lead back for a Packers team struggling to get anything going on the ground. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Tuesday that it is " way too early " to determine whether Reed will play again in 2026. That said, he was not placed on injured reserve ahead of their Week 3 contest. He will reportedly undergo surgery . Impact: Beyond the football implications, it is good to hear Reed avoided any life-altering injuries in Week 2. Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are likely to soak up additional snaps, although volume is most likely to concentrate on Christian Watson , Matthew Golden , and Tucker Kraft . Chris Brooks - RB (ankle) Brooks suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 4 win over the Buccaneers and is reportedly undergoing further testing. He did not practice on Wednesday and was ruled out f or Week 5 on Friday. Impact: Brooks had been the most consistent rusher in a timeshare situation. Kaleb Johnson lost another fumble in Week 4, leaving MarShawn Lloyd as the likely beneficiary for as long as Brooks remains sidelined, although that role carries little value for the team with the fewest rush attempts in the league through the first month of the season. Skyy Moore - WR (ankle) Moore sported a walking boot instead of practicing on Wednesday . He was ruled out for Week 6 Friday . Impact: Should he miss time, the Packers' star players would further consolidate touches. ◆ Minnesota Vikings Jordan Addison - WR (hamstring) Addison did not practice on Wednesday due to “ a little hamstring soreness .” He was listed as questionable for Week 5, ultimately unable to go. Impact: Justin Jefferson remains the alpha in this offense. Jordan Mason - RB (thumb) The Vikings placed Mason on injured reserve in Week 2 . The team reportedly “ hopes ” to get him back in Week 7. Impact: The Vikings are on bye in Week 6, so Mason will be eligible to return in Week 7. Starting running back Aaron Jones gets a deserved projections boost with Mason sidelined. Veteran RB DeeJay Dallas operated as the RB3. Rookie RB Demond Claiborne can be stashed on benches. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. NFC South ◆ Atlanta Falcons Michael Penix - QB (ribs) Penix suffered a ribs injury late in the fourth quarter of the team's overtime loss to the Ravens in Week 5. He is practicing in full for Week 6 and was removed from the injury report Friday . Impact: Penix is good to go this week, and can be started as a high-end QB2 with four teams on bye. ◆ Carolina Panthers Jalen Coker - WR (quadricep) Coker suffered a quad injury in Week 3 that forced him to depart the game. He did not play in Week 4. Head coach Dave Canales said Monday that Coker is "on track" for Week 6 against the Eagles. He is practicing in full for Week 6 . Impact: He is a WR2 against the Eagles. Darren Waller - TE (toe) Waller was limited to begin Week 6 . Impact: Waller should be able to handle his normal workload. Ideally, he practices in full by the end of the week. Jonathan Brooks - RB (groin) Brooks aggravated the groin injury that forced him to miss the end of camp. The Panthers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. He is expected to undergo core muscle surgery . Impact: Chuba Hubbard enters the volume-driven RB1 discussion in Brooks' absence. Trevor Etienne ( ankle ) is practicing in full and can be stashed in 14-team leagues, while AJ Dillon was ruled out. ◆ New Orleans Saints Tyler Shough - QB (left hand) Shough injured his non-throwing hand . He was limited on Wednesday but removed from the injury report Friday . He is practicing in full for Week 6. Impact: It will not impact his throwing ability. Chris Olave - WR (illness) Olave did not practice on Wednesday and drew a questionable tag for Week 6. Impact: Although listed as questionable, we fully expect Olave to play against the Giants. Travis Etienne - RB (hamstring) Etienne aggravated his hamstring injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Raiders. Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that he expects Etienne to "miss some time." Impact: Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller appear likely to split the load in Etienne's absence, neither of whom is overly enticing in fantasy circles in what is expected to be a shared workload. Alvin Kamara - RB (back) Kamara played through the injury ineffectively last week. He remains limited to begin Week 6 , ultimately drawing the questionable tag. Impact: Kamara is entirely touchdown-dependent. Jordyn Tyson - WR (hamstring) Tyson begins the regular season on injured reserve . He could return in Week 7 . Impact: Devaughn Vele should begin the season in the starting lineup opposite Chris Olave , with both players routinely used in the slot. Olave's weekly range of outcomes rivals almost any receiver in the league for as long as Tyson remains out, while tight end Juwan Johnson should return weekly TE1 finishes. ◆ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Jalen McMillan - WR (knee) McMillan suffered a sprained PCL in his first game action of the season in Week 3. The team placed him on injured reserve Monday, with an expected absence of 6-8 weeks. Impact: Not much change considering he made his season debut in Week 3, although rookie Ted Hurst should remain in the starting lineup. Baker Mayfield - QB (thumb) Mayfield suffered a dislocated thumb in the team's Week 3 loss to the Vikings. He is expected to be sidelined for three-to-six weeks . As of Week 6, he has not resumed throwing . Impact: Undrafted free agent rookie Jalon Daniels will start in Mayfield's absence. Daniels went undrafted for a reason, the primary of which was his inconsistencies as a passer. Consider it a significant downgrade for Emeka Egbuka , Chris Godwin , Ted Hurst , and Cade Otton . NFC West ◆ Arizona Cardinals Jeremiyah Love - RB (ankle) Love is not practicing early in Week 6 . The team lists him with just one ankle injury despite recent reports indicating that his preseason ankle injury remains problematic and he injured his other ankle in Week 4. He was ruled out for Week 6 Friday. Impact: Tyler Allgeier can now be started as a viable FLEX option in the absence of Love. ◆ Los Angeles Rams Terrance Ferguson - TE (ankle) Ferguson aggravated an ankle injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Broncos. Head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Ferguson is likely to miss Week 4. He did not practice on Wednesday and was sent to injured reserve Friday. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: Colby Parkinson (shoulder) is playing through his injury and Davis Allen (foot) is sidelined. Tyler Higbee is a viable TE1 in fantasy. ◆ San Francisco 49ers Mike Evans - WR (ribs, Achilles) Evans did not practice Thursday or Friday and drew a questionable designation for Week 6. Impact: Likely none. Evans continues to play through multiple ailments and should see a normal workload against the Commanders. Even so, fantasy managers could look to make alternate plans considering the timing of the 49ers' game. Demarcus Robinson - WR (ankle) Robinson suffered a high-ankle sprain in the team's Week 2 win over the Dolphins. He will miss significant time. Impact : Reports suggest Jacob Cowing will be leaned on to fill the void left behind by the injuries to Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling . Expect Mike Evans , assuming health, Christian McCaffrey , and George Kittle to soak up additional volume. Deebo Samuel - WR (hamstring) Samuel suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 5 win over the Seahawks. He is expected to miss multiple weeks and was ruled out for Week 6 Saturday. Impact: The Athletic's Matt Barrows believes Brandin Cooks is the "next man up" for a 49ers team absolutely devastated by injuries. Cooks can be added from waivers after serving as the de facto WR2 opposite Mike Evans once Samuel departed. De’Zhaun Stribling - WR (ankle) Stribling suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 1 win over the Rams. The 49ers placed him on injured reserve in Week 2 after he underwent surgery to repair a deltoid ligament tear. He is expected to return in 10 weeks. Impact: The Athletic's Matt Barrows believes Demarcus Robinson will be the primary beneficiary. Ricky Pearsall - WR (knee) Pearsall was placed on season-ending injured reserve. Impact: Pearsall will miss the entirety of the 2026 season. ◆ Seattle Seahawks Zach Charbonnet - RB (knee) Charbonnet begins the season on the physically unable to perform list, although the team remains optimistic he will be able to beat his initial recovery timeline. He reportedly has a " legitimate chance " to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs. Impact: Charbonnet could return to a sizable role when healthy. Jadarian Price - RB (chest) Price was placed on injured reserve in Week 4. Impact: Price played through the injury in Week 3 but apparently emerged worse off for wear. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani will split the backfield in his absence, although the biggest boost likely falls back to Jaxon Smith-Njigba . Jaxon Smith-Njigba - WR (ankle) Smith-Njigba is cleared to play in Week 6 against the Broncos. Impact: None.

stories.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) expected to play vs. Falcons in Week 6
stories.summary: Williams has been sidelined since Week 2.
stories.detailText: The Chicago Bears expect to have their starting quarterback available for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Saturday afternoon that Caleb Williams has had no setbacks, and all signs point to him starting Sunday. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Williams has been sidelined for the last three weeks. The Chicago QB suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings. When Williams went down at the end of the game, his reaction led many to worry he would miss significant time. He was diagnosed with a hamstring strain, but it was still enough to sideline him for three weeks. Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum managed a 2-1 record in his absence. In two games this season, Williams has thrown for 407 yards, 2 touchdowns and 1 interception. The quarterback has used his legs well this season, picking up 107 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Chicago is 3-2 and coming off a loss to the Green Bay Packers. Bagent got the start, but he struggled to figure out the Packers' defense. The team benched him in the second half in favor of Keenum. Bagent's last drive ended in an interception before halftime. Keenum's first second-half drive ended with an interception in the end zone. The veteran Keenum was the hero in Chicago's Week 4 blowout of the Philadelphia Eagles. Against Green Bay, though, Keenum finished 11 of 19 passing for 108 yards with an interception and a fumble lost. Bagent was 12 of 21 for just 21 yards with two picks. Williams began the week participating fully in practice including Thursday and Friday, but was still listed as questionable heading into the weekend. With no reported setbacks, he is expected to be under center against the Falcons on Sunday. Chicago opted not to add Williams to injured reserve after his injury. If they had, he wouldn't be eligible to play this week. Head coach Ben Johnson is known for being crafty with his game plan, so he could trot Bagent out for the first play and then swap in Williams, but regardless, it sounds like Chicago has its starting QB back.

stories.summary: Week 6 updates.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 04: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during a game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced four roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers. Here’s an overview: QB Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve. RB Jaydon Blue was signed from the practice squad to the roster. EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby and S Cole Wisniewski were temporarily elevated from the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. JALEN HURTS On Saturday morning, ESPN reported that the Eagles were NOT going to place Hurts on injured reserve. On Saturday afternoon, ESPN reported that the Eagles are putting Hurts on IR after all. Breaking: After consultations with numerous doctors and experts that went into Saturday, the #Eagles are placing quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, sources tell @AdamSchefter and me. Hurts is now out for the foreseeable future. More information coming… pic.twitter.com/EHDeVw0Nye — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 17, 2026 By going on IR due to his “superficial blood clot,” Hurts is now out for at least the Eagles’ next four games: Week 6 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars Week 7 vs. Dallas Cowboys Week 8 at Washington Commanders Week 9 vs. New York Giants The Eagles then have a bye in Week 10. The earliest Hurts could possibly return is for the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The uncertain nature of Hurts’ situation makes it hard to predict exactly when he’ll be back. In the meantime, the Eagles will roll with Tanner McKee as their starting quarterback. It’ll be interesting to see how he fares in his first-ever extended NFL action. Cole Payton will likely be the backup for Week 6 since Joe Milton III only joined the team on Friday. To be determined if Milton will eventually overtake Payton or if he’ll just be the emergency third quarterback option. JAYDON BLUE With Saquon Barkley still dealing with a hamstring injury and both Tank Bigsby/Will Shipley now on injured reserve, the Eagles are currently without their top three running backs. Last week, the team called Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele up from the practice squad. Now Blue is joining them on the roster to give the Eagles three backfield options for Sunday’s game. The Eagles originally signed Blue, a former Cowboys draft pick, prior to the 2026 season. KEYSHAWN JAMES-NEWBY The Eagles are currently banged up at edge rusher. Jalyx Hunt was ruled out for Sunday’s game while A.J. Epenesa is doubtful to play. Jonathan Greenard will play while coming off an ankle injury. And so the team decided to temporarily elevate KJN to make his NFL debut. The rookie seventh-round pick missed most of the Eagles’ offseason practices due to injury but he flashed a little late in training camp and in the preseason. KJN will likely be most limited to special teams duty, barring more edge rusher injuries. Not necessarily surprising but a little interesting to see the Eagles elevated KJN instead of fellow practice squad edge rusher Mason Reiger. COLE WISNIEWSKI Wisniewski, another member of the Eagles’ 2026 NFL Draft class, is set to make his NFL regular season debut as a depth safety and special teams contributor. The Eagles are currently thin at safety. Andrew Mukuba and Cooper DeJean are the starters in base defense with Marcus Epps playing next to Mukuba in nickel packages. Epps is returning from injury this week after previously losing some snaps to Michael Carter II, who was ruled out of Sunday’s game. The Eagles also have Kenny Moore II, who is transitioning to safety after mostly playing nickel cornerback prior to coming to Philly. Wisniewski gives the Eagles another option on the back end of the defense in a pinch. NOTABLE NON-MOVES The Eagles did NOT temporarily elevate Zach Ertz to the roster. Ertz maxed out on elevations with three since he returned to Philly after Week 2. Ertz is now only eligible to play for the Eagles if they sign him to their roster. The Eagles also did NOT activate Landon Dickerson, Eli Stowers, Grant Calcaterra, or Jakorian Bennett from injured reserve. The team opened their 21-day practice windows to return from IR earlier this week.

(Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pro Bowl wide receiver A.J. Brown will make his official return versus the New York Jets after spending four games on injured reserve. But the New England Patriots announced an additional two moves on the eve of the AFC East meeting at Gillette Stadium. The organization elevated safety Elliott Davison for Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET kickoff and also released running back Hassan Haskins from the practice squad. Davison, 24, reverted last week after appearing in his first NFL game beyond the preseason. The 6-foot, 190-pound safety recorded two tackles and one pass deflection during what became a 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. He handled 10 snaps on defense and 19 snaps on special teams in his debut as a standard elevation and now has a third and final call-up remaining before a move to the active roster would be required to take the field. Signed to the Patriots’ practice squad at the start of September before being released and re-signed , Davison originally entered the league as an undrafted free agent out of UTSA in 2025. The former Roadrunners defensive back logged all of his rookie year on the practice squad of the New Orleans Saints and cleared waivers following the 53-man cutdown deadline in August. Haskins, 26, departs from New England’s practice squad after returning to the fold last week. The 6-foot-2, 228-pound running back had visited Foxborough for a workout that became a contract ahead of the preseason opener. After being released as a vested veteran at the end of August, he spent two weeks on the initial practice squad before circling back amid October. Selected in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL draft at No. 131 overall, Haskins spent previous tours with the Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers. Through 44 games, the Michigan product stands with 76 carries for 229 yards, 18 catches for 119 yards, three touchdowns as well as one start in the backfield. He has handled 371 snaps on offense and 683 snaps on special teams in his career. The Patriots recently worked out three running backs and move forward with a full 53-man roster as well as one open spot on the 17-man practice squad. Any player who is fined three times for one of five player safety rules — horse-collar tackles, launching and blindside blocks are the others — is subject to a one-game suspension.

Brown was activated from injured reserve Saturday after missing the past four games with a right high ankle sprain, the team announced. Brown was limited throughout the week of practice, according to the Patriots' injury report, and he will likely be eased back into the mix before taking on his usual heavy workload. That comes after a previous ESPN report said the Eagles hadn’t even discussed putting Hurts on injured reserve. stories.title: Jalen Hurts placed on IR due to blood clot
stories.summary: The Eagles QB will be out for the critical game vs. the Panthers.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images Update: On Saturday, news broke that the Philadelphia Eagles have placed Jalen Hurts on Injured Reserve due to the blood clot in his calf. He will now miss at least the next four games. Read on for more. Previously: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss his Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers after the team announced Thursday that he has a small “superficial blood clot” in his calf, and that the team is keeping him out due to an abundance of caution after there appeared to be movement with the clot. A full statement was released by the team via Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network , which reads: On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report. Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team’s flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia. Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter. On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority. The Week 6 game was shaping up as a must-win for the Eagles in order to get their season back on track, but that will be considerably more difficult with the news that the team will be without Hurts. Philadelphia’s depth chart at quarterback is extremely thin, with Tanner McKee expected to make the start. Drafted in the 6th round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Stanford, McKee has appeared in six career games, where he completed 61.4% of his passes for 597 yards and 5 TDs. While the QB has been decent in limited time, this will be his first time starting since Week 17 of 2024, when the Eagles rested their starters against a 3-13 Giants team. Of course, the football side of this is the least important part. This is a scary, potentially life-threatening injury that was caught early by the Eagles and they have made the best possible move for Hurts’ health. We now wait to see how significant this injury is moving forward, and whether or not it will cause Hurts to miss additional games.

The Philadelphia Eagles will NOT be placing Jalen Hurts on injured reserve while the starting quarterback recovers from a “ superficial blood clot ,” according to a report from ESPN . Not yet , at least. Bold emphasis mine: The team, according to sources, has not even discussed the possibility of injured reserve, which would sideline Hurts for a minimum of four weeks. Hurts and the Eagles are still gathering more information and seeking additional medical opinions, with the quarterback’s health the foremost consideration. They believe the blood clot is treatable, with Hurts trying to determine the best course, sources said. The ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, and the Eagles are ready to follow his lead. There is still a chance Hurts eventually ends up on injured reserve, if that is the direction the medical information indicates. The Eagles had until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday, October 17 to put Hurts on IR and have Week 6 count towards one of the four games he would be required to miss before being eligible to be activated. By not putting him on IR, then, the Eagles are keeping the door open that he can play in Week 9 by the latest. However, a clear timeline for Hurts’ recovery doesn’t seem to exist. At least not publicly. And this report acknowledges that Hurts might eventually end up on IR. On one hand, I can understand the Eagles not putting Hurts on IR. It wouldn’t be ideal if he ended up being fine sooner than expected but he couldn’t play due to IR mechanics. I’m guessing Hurts doesn’t want to be placed on IR right now and that sentiment is relevant to the Eagles’ decision. On the other hand, I wish the Eagles would put Hurts on IR in an effort to avoid any unrealistic expectations about him returning sooner than many would hope. The Eagles could also use the roster spot. With a retired Lane Johnson counting towards the limit all season long, the Eagles are already operating with a 52-player roster. And if Hurts is taking up a spot while missing a lot of games, it’ll effectively be a 51-player limit. We’ll see if the Eagles end up changing their minds down the road.

stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- Chicago Bears nickel corner Kyler Gordon has been activated off the physically unable to perform list and onto the 53-man roster, the team announced Saturday. Gordon spent the offseason rehabbing a calf injury that landed him on the PUP list at the start of training camp. He was moved to reserve/PUP on Aug. 30 and had to sit out the Bears' first four games. He returned to practice Sept. 30 and has been a full participant in every session over the past three weeks. "He's done a great job taking everything that we've assigned him so far," coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "I feel good about him -- whether that's this week or next week -- I do feel good about him being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there's a number of ways he can do that. But I'm encouraged with what I've seen so far." In a corresponding move, the Bears placed defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve. Odeyingbo had already been ruled out for Week 6 with a quad injury sustained against the Green Bay Packers last week. Coach Ben Johnson said this week that Odeyingbo was expected to miss "some time" but that the Bears did not believe his injury was serious enough to warrant IR. The Bears also released Xavier Woods , who started the last two games at safety, and signed defensive back Nick McCloud from the practice squad to the active roster. Gordon was drafted 39th overall in 2022, the very first pick by Bears general manager Ryan Poles. Since then, the cornerback has totaled five interceptions, 17 passes defensed, 2.5 sacks, 10 tackles for loss and two forced fumbles. Injuries were present during his first three seasons (2022-24) but did not stop the Bears from making him the NFL's highest-paid primary slot corner in April 2025 when he signed a three-year, $40 million extension with $31.25 million guaranteed. Since signing his new deal, Gordon has struggled to stay on the field. He was limited to five games, including the playoffs, in 2025 due to multiple soft tissue injuries and spent two separate stints on injured reserve. Last season, Gordon allowed 16 receptions on 24 targets for 243 yards and three touchdowns, according to Next Gen Stats. He allowed a passer rating of 139.4 in coverage, which was the third highest in the NFL among cornerbacks (minimum 20 targets), with only Trevon Diggs (154.6) and McCloud (142.2) allowing a higher passer rating. After being sidelined for the Bears' offseason program and training camp, Gordon spent several weeks away from the team in September rehabbing on his own. He returned to Halas Hall ahead of Week 4 and made an impression on his coaches for how quickly he got up to speed on the practice field and in meetings. "The one thing about Kyler, he's a sharp kid, or young man, I should say," Bears nickels coach Cannon Matthews said. "So that part I'm not worried about. Even just him being back in meetings, the questions that he asks has always been great that way. So honestly, there's still area for growth in that department, but I don't have any issue with him getting caught up to speed with the mental aspect." The Bears could use some reinforcements in the secondary after Packers quarterback Jordan Love had six completions of 25-plus yards in Chicago's 31-7 loss. Gordon has not played since the Bears- Rams divisional playoff matchup in January, so it is unrealistic to think he could play a full workload of 50 to 70 snaps, according to defensive coordinator Dennis Allen. "I've said this before, I think that Kyler can help us win games," Allen said. "You know, when that time comes where he's able to be out there on the field and participate and help us win games, I'm looking forward to that time."

stories.title: Broncos' Jonathon Cooper off commissioner exempt list, could return Week 7
stories.summary: Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper was removed from the commissioner exempt list Friday, meaning he's available to play in Week 7. Cooper, who was arrested twice in a seven-day span in June on domestic violence charges, has been on the list since Aug. 30.
stories.detailText: ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- NFL commissioner Roger Goodell removed Denver Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the league's exempt list Friday. Cooper, who was unable to practice or play in games while he was on the list, will now be available to play in the Broncos' Week 7 road game against the Arizona Cardinals . Cooper, who was arrested twice in a seven-day span in June on domestic violence charges , has been on the exempt list since Aug. 30. He was in Douglas County (Colo.) court last week for a motions hearing and has a March 2-4 trial scheduled in his case, with a pretrial hearing set for Feb. 19. In a statement Friday, the NFL said its review of Cooper's case "remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Cooper's roster status." Cooper could still face league discipline at a later date under the NFL's personal conduct policy. The Broncos will get a one-week roster exemption for Cooper, who can now return to practice. He could be added to the 53-man roster at any point over the next week and play Oct. 25 against the Cardinals. He had been able to attend meetings and other team functions, including weight room and conditioning work, when he was on the exempt list. The exempt list is designed to remove a player from participation in games and practices while potential violations of the personal conduct policy are reviewed. Cooper has been paid while on the list. His time on the exempt list -- the first six weeks of the regular season -- would count toward any league-mandated suspension in the future. If suspended, however, he would have to return the weekly game checks he has received because suspensions from the personal conduct policy are without pay. Cooper had practiced throughout training camp. Cooper faces a felony charge of second-degree assault by strangulation and three misdemeanors, including violating a protection order, after he was arrested June 4 and then again June 11 after incidents involving his girlfriend. The felony charge stemmed from the first arrest after the results of a forensic examination of Cooper's girlfriend by a nurse. The affidavit that was included in the police investigation into Cooper's first arrest contained the report from the medical exam of Cooper's girlfriend. In it, a nurse wrote that the woman experienced a physical injury from being choked that led to a "substantial risk of death" or substantial risk of injury, including the possibility of traumatic brain injury. Broncos coach Sean Payton has consistently deferred to the NFL's investigation and the legal process when he has discussed the team's approach with the sixth-year linebacker. Payton said that the Broncos set guidelines for Cooper after the arrest and that that has included therapy. Cooper was a seventh-round pick in the 2021 draft and has 31.5 sacks in 81 career games with the Broncos, including eight sacks last season. He has started every game in each of the past three seasons. The Broncos are 4-2 after Thursday night's home win over the Seattle Seahawks .

For the Ravens, he's 6-7 with three straight wins. On Friday, Browns safety Grant Delpit addressed some of the similarities between Huntley and two-time MVP Lamar Jackson. Delpit then was asked to identify the biggest difference. " One is Lamar Jackson ," Delpit said. He's right. But Huntley has proven to be capable. Last week, he completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions. He added 20 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground. So while he's not Lamar (no one is), Huntley can do enough. Delpit's acknowledgement of the obvious could give Huntley a little extra incentive to prove that the gap may not be quite as large as Delpit thinks. The stakes are high. A win by Cleveland (which would be their fourth straight in the AFC North, a first since 1987) would tie the Ravens and Browns at 4-2. A loss would give Baltimore a two-game lead over the Browns and the first half of the head-to-head tiebreaker.

stories.title: New York Jets make roster moves ahead of New England Patriots game
stories.summary: The Jets get a key part of their passing game back for Sunday’s clash with the Patriots
stories.detailText: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Omar Cooper Jr. #11 of the New York Jets runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets will be activating rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. from the injured reserve list for this Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots. They will also be elevating linebacker Jaden Keller from the practice squad. Omar Cooper is a 6’ 0”, 200 pound receiver out of Indiana University. He was drafted by the Jets with the 30th overall pick in the 1st round of the 2026 NFL draft. Cooper has had a bit of a rough start to his NFL career. In training camp Cooper briefly fell behind Isaiah Williams to the fourth receiver on the depth chart. That didn’t last long, and Cooper entered the season as the WR3 behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell. It took only five NFL snaps for Cooper to make a splash, as he pinballed his way to a spectacular 30 yard catch and run on the Jets’ first drive of the 2026 season. It was an electrifying start to Cooper’s NFL career. Unfortunately, that was the last snap Cooper would see until the upcoming game against the New England Patriots. Cooper was injured on the play and was immediately removed from the game. He was placed on the injured reserve list and has spent the last four games there. On Sunday Cooper will try to pick up where he left off and give the Jets a boost in the passing game. With Adonai Mitchell out for this game Cooper will be a welcome sight on the field. Jaden Keller is a 23 year old, 6’ 3”, 235 pound linebacker out of Virginia Tech. He went undrafted in 2026 and the Jets signed him as an undrafted free agent before releasing him prior to the start of the regular season and adding him to the practice squad. Keller made his NFL debut two weeks ago when the Jets elevated him from the practice squad. In two games with the Jets Keller has played 39 snaps, all on special teams, and recorded one tackle. Sunday will mark Keller’s third elevation from the practice squad this season. Teams are limited to elevating any player three times in any given season. After this game if the Jets wish to activate Keller on Sundays they will need to sign him to the 53 man roster.

stories.title: Instant Recap: Michigan State blows 8-point lead, loses to NW 24-21
stories.summary: The Spartans give up 11 unanswered points in the last eight minutes.
stories.detailText: Michigan State’s head coach Pat Fitzgerald high five players after MSU blocked a Northwestern field goal during the second quarter on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Just when you thought Pat Fitzgerald was going to get his first Big Ten win as head coach of the Spartans, the rug was pulled out from underneath them in the final minute. The game started out slow as Michigan State would fail a fourth-down conversion on their opening drive, but Alessio Milivojevic was strip-sacked after a Northwestern three-and-out that put the Wildcats in the redzone instantly. MSU was able to hold them to a field goal after NW recovered an Aidan Chiles fumble, and a 39-yard attempt gave the Cats a 3-0 lead. After a big kick return across midfield by Kenneth Williams, the Spartans responded. They converted two fourth downs in the redzone, including one from the three-yard line that resulted in a Milivojevic rushing touchdown to give MSU the lead 7-3 before the end of the first quarter. At the start of the second, a nice Northwestern drive ended with a 10-yard rushing touchdown by Caleb Komolafe. The Cats were able to reclaim the lead 10-7. Milivojevic’s play was turning a corner with some impressive throws downfield, including a 29-yard pass on the ensuing possession, but he overthrew a wide-open Rodney Bullard Jr which would’ve resulted in a 40-yard touchdown pass. Luckily for MSU, a dropped Northwestern catch in the endzone forced the Cats to kick a field goal, but Eli Coenen got a hand on the kick to block the attempt and give some momentum back to the offense. On the final drive of the half, Bullard dropped a tough catch in the endzone that bounced off his fingertips, but Milivojevic made the exact same throw on the next play and found Bryson Williams on a back-shoulder catch to reclaim the lead. Michigan State would head into halftime with a 14-10 lead over Northwestern. There wasn’t much offense for either team in the third quarter, but the one time NW was able to get into the redzone, MSU came up with another defensive stop to force a field goal, and the Spartans held a 14-13 lead heading into the fourth quarter. That’s when Big Play McCray showed up. Chrishon McCray caught a NW punt inside the ten-yard line, but a 41-yard return helped Michigan State start their next drive from midfield. Just two plays later, Milivojevic found McCray for a 53-yard touchdown pass on a deep ball down the middle to make it a 21-13 Spartans lead. It didn’t take long for Northwestern to respond as they put together their best drive of the day that finished with a one-yard touchdown run for Chiles. Chiles was able to find Alex Honig for the two-point conversion, and the Cats tied it up at 21 with a little over seven minutes left. Milivojevic would again miss Bullard on an overthrow that would’ve resulted in a touchdown, but the Cats’ coaching staff gifted the Spartans with one of the worst fake punt calls I’ve ever seen. It failed horribly for Northwestern, and MSU took over on the Northwestern 28-yard line. The Spartans were instantly in field goal range. And yet, with a minute left, Liam Boyd’s 33-yard field goal attempt was blocked. It took less than a minute for Chiles and Northwestern to drive 64 yards back the other way, and they converted on their field goal with two seconds left to win 24-21. This team has found multiple ways to put themselves in positions to win, yet they can’t close games. Alessio missed at least three deep throws that should’ve resulted in touchdowns. The defensive line finally got to the quarterback in this one with four sacks just from Ben Roberts and Anelu Lafaele. It was an impressive game on both sides of the ball, but they didn’t do enough late in clutch time to get the job done. Michigan State will travel to California next weekend to take on Bob Chesney and the #12 UCLA Bruins. Go Green!

Texas quarterback Arch Manning, who until recently was the betting favorite to go first overall in next year's draft, had another bad game. Manning had been up and down throughout, but when Texas got the ball back down by three with two and a half minutes to play, it looked like an opportunity for Manning to engineer a great comeback. Instead, Manning was sacked and fumbled, Florida recovered, and that was that. Florida won, 27-24. The other top draft prospect on the Longhorns, Texas pass rusher Colin Simmons, the NCAA leader in sacks and a potential Top 5 pick in 2027, was carted off with a left leg injury in the fourth quarter. Manning has been known to make big plays with his legs at times, but he couldn't do that today against Florida. In one particularly rough sequence, Manning attempted to run for a first down on third-and-1 but lost a yard. Texas then went for it on fourth-and-2, Manning again tried to run, and he again was tackled behind the line of scrimmage for a turnover on downs. He also repeatedly failed to escape pass pressure. Florida running back Jadan Baugh, considered by some the best running back prospect in the 2027 draft class, scored the fourth-quarter winning touchdown for the Gators. He finished with 25 carries for 91 yards. But the story of the game will be Manning, who has failed to live up to the hype. This was an ugly performance, following an ugly performance in last week's loss to Oklahoma, and it's fair to question whether Manning is a future NFL star, or whether he just shares the same last name as three past NFL stars.

teamStories.summary: Returning Raider Nation’s questions for the week.
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s funny how two weeks can dramatically change the tune of an entire season. The Las Vegas Raiders have gone from a feel-good story as one of the biggest surprises in the NFL to feeling like the sky is falling. Back-to-back losses, including an embarrassing blowout in New England last week, will do that. Part of the reason is the Raiders’ offensive line continues to be an issue, as it’s a major point of emphasis in this week’s mailbag (again) heading into Week 6 against the Buffalo Bills . Q: I’ve seen a couple of other guys on Raider Twitter saying that Spencer Burford has been the best guard still, and his PFF grades are more affected because they mostly help the other side. Sorta similar to DJ Glaze. I think Marcus, in one of the TDLs, said he was the best run blocker for that game. He seems to get beat a lot in pass pro every game, though. What do you think about that? Do you feel run or pass pro is more important and that affects the choice? It kinda seems like the guards have all been bad, but at some point the decision is if they are gonna be bad anyway, then you might as well work on the upside of Caleb Rogers or Trey Zuhn III. Also, if the Raiders are gonna throw Fernando Mendoza in there, they’ve gotta protect him better, right? A: When it comes to pass protection versus run blocking at guard, I tend to lean toward the running game . Of course, both are requirements of the position. However, in my opinion, pass protection is easiest at guard — compared to the other two offensive line positions — since they (typically) aren’t responsible for setting the protection and doing the thinking for a group like a center is. Also, guards have help on both sides with a center and a tackle to their left and right, and interior pass-rushers don’t have as much space to operate, unlike blocking on the edge. So while it’s ideal to have a guard who can do both at a high level, personally, I’ll sacrifice some pass-pro issues for a high-level run blocker. Burford is decent in the running game and has had a couple of good outings in that department. For some context, Pro Football Focus gave him a 73.9 run-blocking grade against the Saints and an 81.0 against the Chiefs. One of those two is the game Marcus referenced. However, Burford has a 56.6 mark for the season. To be clear, I’m not trying to say PFF grades are the end-all, be-all; I’m just using them to contextualize the level of “good” versus “bad” and Burford’s performance. The problem is, and this is true pretty much regardless of what website or metric you’re using, he’s given up the most pressures ( 18 ) of any guard in the league and has the fourth-lowest pass protection grade (26.6). To me, just being decent or slightly above-average as a run blocker isn’t worth the liability he’s been when protecting the quarterback, even given my preference for the position. Also, as you mentioned, Mendoza is going to take over at some point. Having a young quarterback shifts the goalposts because putting the future of the franchise behind bad pass protection is organizational malpractice. That’s where even I would say it makes more sense to give a guy like Zuhn, who doesn’t bring much as a run blocker but was good in pass protection at tackle in college, so the rookie signal-caller doesn’t get killed. I think the narrative that Burford was getting less help was true during the first three weeks of the season. However, in the last two games, he’s been getting a lot more help from Kolton Miller in pass protection. When the Raiders want to push the ball down the field, Miller has been staying closer to the line of scrimmage a little longer so that he can help slow the defensive tackle down. More on this in the next question; that’s also part of the left tackle’s issues. At the end of the day, both guards have left something to be desired. Jackson Powers-Johnson continues to be inconsistent, especially as a run blocker, but he’s at least been solid in pass protection. So, he and Burford both could get replaced, and it wouldn’t surprise me if Klint Kubiak does that soon. But, in my opinion, Kubiak at least has to give someone else a shot at left guard. The thing to keep in mind about Burford is that the only reason he started games during his last two years in San Francisco was because of injuries. On top of that, Ben Bartch was the 49ers’ starting left guard in Weeks 1 and 2 before getting injured, and they turned to Connor Colby before Burford after Bartch went down last season. I get the “scheme fit” and “familiarity with the system” line of thinking, but Burford didn’t have the track record to be unchallenged for the starting spot in training camp. If you ask me, it’s time for Kubiak to try someone else at that spot. Q: What is going on with Kolton Miller? Is he injured, or is FatherTime finally catching up with him? A: I got this question last week and defended Miller, saying he only had one bad game at the time. Then, he went out and had another bad game. (Thanks for having my back, Kolton, LOL!). So, I definitely think left tackle is something to monitor for the rest of the year, especially as we creep closer to the offseason and start thinking about team needs. The 31-year-old likely doesn’t have that many years left, after all, and he certainly needs to play better. However, picking up where I left off above, I don’t think it’s a coincidence that Miller’s struggles began the week after Burford gave up a season-high six pressures and posted a 4.0 PFF pass-blocking grade against the Saints. As previously mentioned, the left tackle has been giving the guard more help in pass protection, and the clip Marcus posted below is a good example. This was a bad sack by Cousins. He had Tucker open, and I'm not sure why he came off it. Then just stares down Bowers. Knocked the Raiders out of field goal range. pic.twitter.com/qt56gT2KwL — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) October 12, 2026 The endzone view (which starts around the 20-second mark) gives you a good look at what I’m talking about when I say Miller has to stay closer to the line of scrimmage at first. Notice how he doesn’t get much depth on his pass set initially and extends his inside arm. That’s to give the defensive tackle (No. 97) less space to operate and potentially get another hand on the DT to help slow his momentum down for Burford. Compare Miller’s pass set to DJ Glaze’s on the other side. Since the center is turning to the right and able to help JPJ, Glaze doesn’t have to worry about assisting the guard and can get depth immediately. Whereas Miller has to hang tight for a second and then rush to get depth, throwing his footwork and the whole process out of whack because the process has to be sped up. On top of that, Burford loses on the high side of the rush, forcing Kirk Cousins to step up in the pocket. As a result, the edge rusher works back inside and Miller, who can’t see where the quarterback is, gives up a sack. Don’t get me wrong, Miller has to do a better job of staying engaged on the block and staying in front of inside moves is part of playing tackle. But the point I’m making here is that his assignment is more difficult because the guy next to him isn’t getting the job done. So, both guards are getting help in this example. However, one of them was brought in to be a reliable veteran who knows the system, and the other had to fight to retain his starting spot during training camp. Again, a case could be made for both guys to get replaced, but I don’t know how anyone can justify Burford’s level of play this season. And when it comes to Miller, he definitely needs to pick it up, too. But I’d like to see how he plays with someone else next to him. Q: I like outside zone running, but maybe the line, which we thought was suited for it, really isn’t. Why not move JPJ to left guard, where he had played better in the past, and try Evan Neal at right guard and run more power/gap? We need some beef on the O-line! A: The Raiders’ rushing attack has been pretty balanced this season, with 60 zone runs to 57 gap runs, according to Sumer Sports . Also, every starting offensive lineman has a better PFF run-blocking grade in zone than gap. Based on that data, the latter is the bigger problem. But to your point about moving Powers-Johnson to the left side, I think that should be on the table, too. He played well there as a rookie, and Caleb Rogers can slide in at right guard since that’s where Rogers has been getting reps. I have my doubts that Neal is the answer, but I’ll take just about anyone other than Burford at this point. At the end of the day, a change just has to be made because the Raiders can’t continue to have such a lackluster rushing attack. Q: Are the OL issues because of mismatched players/scheme fits, that haven’t played together long enough, or coaching that isn’t resonating with the players? At times they look lost out there. A: I’ve touched on most of this already, but the chemistry piece is a factor, too. The interior three have never worked together before this season, and while JPJ and Glaze were in the same draft class, they’ve hardly been next to each other. Powers-Johnson played left guard and center as a rookie, and then missed over half of last season. So, there is some validity to the argument that the line needs more time to gel together, especially since zone runs require more cohesion up front. But the clock is also ticking… Q: Can JJ Pegues improve the Raiders’ pass rush? Should they be looking at practice squad DTs and free agents? Their practice squad DTs have potential as NTs but offer limited pass rush upside. I guess it really depends on how low the bar has been set by Jonah Laulu, Thomas Booker IV and Adam Butler. A: For some context here, I posted on X/Twitter earlier this week that Booker has the highest pass-rush win rate of any Raiders defensive tackle so far this season at 8.5%, according to PFF. The problem is he’s recorded the second-fewest pass-rush snaps (63) of the team’s defensive tackles who have played in at least four games, and that rate ranks 48th among defensive tackles league-wide. In other words, the defense is getting almost no pressure from its interior pass-rushers, and Booker isn’t winning frequently enough to simply just play him more. The bigger problem is that Pegues, or any of the other reserve defensive tackles, aren’t going to solve this problem. He’s more of a run defender, as are Brandon Cleveland and Tim Keenan III, as you mentioned. The interior pass-rusher who needs to step up the most is Tonka Hemingway. He has the skill set and has shown a few flashes but isn’t consistent enough right now. Maybe John Spytek and Co. can find a diamond in the rough from another team’s practice squad or a street free agent, but the odds are pretty low. Ultimately, I think this is something that will leak into the offseason, and Spytek needs to do a much better job of prioritizing the position than he has in the past. Q: Maxx doesn’t seem to be having a heavy impact on games even with his “pressures.” Per PFN, Maxx Crosby is tied for 58th in the NFL with a 6.7% pressure-to-sack ratio. Whether or not the Raiders are contending for a playoff spot as we move towards November, if a team offers a 1st, Spy would be crazy not to take it. Would you agree? A: I know some people are getting frustrated with Crosby getting pressures but only having two sacks this season, and I think that comes down to a misunderstanding of what the stats show. Sacks happen when pressure is paired with good coverage. It’s no coincidence that the Broncos led the NFL in sacks during each of the last two seasons while having a two-time All-Pro corner in Patrick Surtain II. So, numbers like pressures and pass-rush win rate are used to isolate how the player is performing outside of the supporting cast. In other words, those figures help answer the question of: “Is Maxx Crosby (or whatever pass-rusher) doing his job?” PFF has Crosby tied for fourth among edge rushers with 30 pressures and fourth outright in win rate (20.9%), while having the second-highest double team rate . He is doing his job while opposing offenses are making it more difficult via chip blocks and sliding the protection to him. That’s on top of the coverage being shaky over the last two weeks, allowing the quarterbacks to find quick answers in the passing game. Also, sacks from edge rushers can come when the defensive tackles force the quarterback to step up in or bail out of the pocket. The clip above that I broke down with Burford and Miller is a good example of that. As I mentioned in my previous answer, that’s not happening in Vegas, either. I get it, a sack is the best stat a pass-rusher can have, and people want to see Crosby at the top of the charts. But there’s a lot more that goes into it than just his performance. As far as a trade goes, it’d still have to be more than just a first-round pick for me to get on board with that. Q: Why do you think Mike Washington Jr. is not getting more reps when it was reported that Kubiak wanted to draft him? A: I think a big part of it is the passing game. Washington wasn’t a good receiver or pass protector at Arkansas, and that has carried over into the NFL. Hence why Dylan Laube got more playing time last week. Also, Washington had a bad game against the Chiefs (Marcus mentioned on TDL that he had a missed or bad read that would have resulted in a touchdown), and I think Kubiak might have overreacted to that in New England. Additionally, being down 28-7 after the first position in the third quarter means the offense doesn’t have enough time left to run the ball much in the second half. The rookie running back’s workload will be something to keep tabs on this Sunday to see if Kubiak makes an adjustment Q: While I know the wide receivers have been a disappointment for not separating in their routes, doesn’t some of the blame go on Kubiak for not being able to “scheme” them open? He seems to be able to scheme Bowers open, and he doesn’t need his help. Other great offensive minds seem able to scheme their guys open all the time. Kubiak has done it a couple of times this year but not very often. A: Kubiak definitely seems to focus on scheming his top offensive weapon open rather than the supporting cast. For example, Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the Seahawks’ leading receiver last year with 119 catches and 1,793 yards, while no other pass-catcher even reached 55 catches and 600 yards during the regular season. So, that seems like one of the play-caller’s shortcomings. But I will say that there have been a decent number of plays where a wide receiver (primarily Tre Tucker) has gotten open, and Kirk Cousins either didn’t have enough time or was staring down Bowers too long. Cousins also has a reputation for checking the ball down quickly, and that’s another factor that can make the wideouts look worse. Now, I will 100% acknowledge that the Raiders have a talent problem at wide receiver, which will likely be another offseason need. But there are external factors like Kubiak and Cousins that have contributed to the lack of production from the position group. We know the current quarterback is a temporary situation, so the bigger factor moving forward is the play caller making some adjustments. Q: Kwity Paye began the season with a great game against Miami (6 tackles and 2 sacks), but it’s been downhill ever since. He had pedestrian performances against the Chargers (2 tackles) and the Saints (3 tackles). His last two games have been abysmal performances against the Chiefs (0 tackles) and the Patriots (1 tackle). I’m interested in your take on Kwity’s weaknesses and what he needs to do to be the impact player that Spytek and Rob Leonard thought he’d be? A: At the end of the day, Paye is a complementary piece rather than a playmaker. He has enough skill and a good motor to clean things up on the defensive line — that’s primarily what he did in the season opener — but isn’t someone who will be consistently productive without contributions from the defense’s main characters. The problem is that type of player isn’t worth $16 million a year. For comparison, Paye is making one million less than Chase Young and Alex Highsmith . Young is the primary pass-rusher in New Orleans and can be productive on his own. Highsmith plays second fiddle to T.J. Watt in Pittsburgh, but he can also win one-on-one matchups and be productive, fitting the second edge-rusher mold perfectly. Now, I mentioned last week that I’ll give Paye some grace since we aren’t even at the halfway point of the season yet. But as the weeks go by and he continues to be underwhelming, that signing continues to get closer and closer to being a bust. Q: Am I wrong for believing John Spytek is part of the problem? His 2025 draft class is looking like a complete bust, and 2026’s draft is looking shaky now. He’s failed to improve the WR room, and his free-agent signings have been suspect at best. A: Someone else asked: What are Spytek’s best and worst moves in the draft and free agency, and what grade would I give him so far? I think a C is a fair assessment for Spytek. Pete Carroll had way too much influence and control over last year’s roster, so I don’t think it’s fair to judge the general manager off the 2025 campaign. On top of that, building a quality roster that is sustainable for the long haul takes several years and draft classes to build, and we haven’t even seen two full seasons during his tenure in Las Vegas. That being said, Spytek has made plenty of Day 2 picks who aren’t seeing the field right now, and free-agent signings like Paye and Jalen Nailor have underwhelming production so far. With that in mind, I’m not going to pound the table and say Spytek has done anything more than an average job, landing on a ‘C’ grade. I know people aren’t going to want to hear this, but I also think Raider Nation needs to be more patient with Spytek. To me, it seems like he wanted to tear the roster down and start the rebuild last year, only to have that plan get blocked by Carroll, forcing him to delay the process by a year. He wasn’t going to fix all the problems and patch all of the holes in one offseason. Remember, expectations were pretty low heading into the season given the lack of talent on the roster. The 3-0 start changed things, but this is still a team that is in year one of a two-year rebuild. As far as best and worst moves: Nakobe Dean has been Spytek’s best free agent signing, and worst was Alex Cappa. Draft picks: I’ll go with Darien Porter for best (Treydan Stukes is a close second), and Charles Grant for worst. Granted, the sample size is the smallest, but I think Porter has been the best corner on the roster this season, and Grant isn’t seeing the field. I’m still a believer in the William & Mary product, but only having 59 snaps from a Top 100 pick is a bad investment so far. Q: There have been even more calls to bench Kirk Cousins since last week, and the team looked dismal versus the Pats as they fell to 3-2. What say you now? A: I still think the move is to roll with Cousins for now. However, if the Raiders lose this week, which I think they will, then the conversation really heats up. The problem is that the Rams are the next team up, and throwing Mendoza behind an offensive line that has been shaky recently against that pass rush probably isn’t a good idea. Plus, at 3-3, the coaching staff can convince themselves that the team is still in playoff contention. So, I think the sweet spot is going to be Week 8 against the Jets, especially if the Raiders drop the next two games. At 3-4 with four straight losses, that would mean Cousins isn’t keeping the playoff hopes alive, so Kubiak would have even more reason to make the change. That would, at least temporarily, help reignite the team’s postseason chances while simultaneously giving the No. 1 about half a season’s worth of starts to build on and grow from moving forward. That’ll do it for this week’s mailbag.
